body_en: 8 Of The World's Largest Widebody Fleets: Who Flies The Most Twin-Aisles?
Louis is a military historian and the staff writer for History of War magazine, a leading military history monthly. He also has an interest in private and commercial aviation.

Recent years have seen the rise of long-haul narrowbody jets, like the Airbus A321XLR , that have killed the hub-and-spoke model by making point-to-point travel between niche destinations possible. However, for the world's premium and legacy airlines, often flying from slot-restricted hubs, the capacity and range of widebody aircraft means that they are still indispensable.

The airlines mentioned in this list of the world's biggest by widebody fleet size have taken many years at the top of their game to amass enormous fleets of huge aircraft. The largest of them is Emirates. However, particularly for the 'big three' US legacy carriers, the widebody fleets are a consequence of a vast overall fleet. These airlines surpass 1,000 aircraft each, with many more single-aisles than widebodies.

According to Planespotters.net , British Airways currently operates a fleet of 299 aircraft. Its widebody aircraft are 18 Airbus A350-1000 and 12 A380-800. It also has 59 777s, divided into 42 777-200 and 16 777-300ER. British Airways' 43 Dreamliners are divided into 12 787-8s, 18 787-9s and 13 787- 10s. This gives a total of 132 twin-aisle jets.

British Airways used to have one of the world's most significant fleets of 747 aircraft. However, these aircraft have not been in the fleet for several years. Retirement due to the COVID-19 pandemic brought half a century of 747 operations, if we include British Airways' precursor, BOAC, to a sudden conclusion in July 2020.

Planespotters.net data shows that American Airlines has 67 Boeing 777s, split between 47 777-200 and 20 777-300ER for a total of 137 twin-aisle aircraft. The carrier also owns 70 Boeing 787 Dreamliners. This includes 37 787-8s and 33 789-9s.

The table below shows the specifications for the 777-300ER, making use of Boeing's technical data . As is seen throughout this article, the 777-300ER is a workhorse that is immensely popular among these carriers.

The American Airlines widebody fleet is a relatively small fraction of the 1,037 aircraft in the fleet. American Airlines' historic widebody fleet includes Boeing 747s and 767s, as well as Airbus A330s.

While British Airways and American Airlines are dominated by narrowbody aircraft, Singapore Airlines is made up of almost exclusively twin-aisle jets. The airline has just 26 Boeing 737s. The table below uses Planespotters.net data to explain the makeup of the widebody fleet, which contains 138 aircraft.

The unique attribute of Singapore Airlines' widebody fleet is its Airbus A350-900ULR, of which it is the exclusive operator. Singapore Airlines uses this jet to fly the world's longest commercial routes currently in operation. These flights have only premium seats, with just premium economy and business class available.

Planespotters.net data reveals a substantial Turkish Airlines twin-aisle fleet of 164 planes. It includes 35 A350-900s, 20 A330-200, and 37 A330-300. In terms of Boeing aircraft, the Turkish flag carrier has 33 777-300ER, 12 777Fs, and 27 787-9 Dreamliners.

Turkish Airlines has plans for enormous fleet expansions in the years to come, with hopes to reach a total fleet size of 800 aircraft by 2036. This will help the carrier to build a network of 350 destinations with an annual revenue of $50 billion, as reported by Simple Flying . As part of Turkish Airlines' efforts to 'premiumize' its fleet, it wants to reintroduce premium economy to its widebody aircraft, starting in 2028.

The airline is examining replacing 8-9% of its current economy cabin with premium economy seats. " Our research shows that around two-thirds of the passengers on long-haul flights are willing to pay a premium for additional legroom and comfort ," its former Chief Commercial Officer Ahmet Olmuştur told Forbes .

As stated by Planespotters.net, the Delta Air Lines' widebody fleet currently includes just three aircraft families, but has reached a fleet of significant size. The fleet has two Airbus families: the A330 (81 jets) and the A350 (42 jets). It has 11 A330-200s, 31 A330-300s and 39 A330-900s. Its A350s are all examples of the A350-900 variant. Delta has just one Boeing widebody family: the 767 (57 jets). These aircraft are divided into 36 767-300ERs and 21 767- 400ERs.

As with American Airlines, this widebody fleet is meager when compared with the narrowbody fleet. Delta has 1006 planes in total, of which just 180 are widebody aircraft. Alone, both Delta's 737 and Airbus A321 fleets are larger than this.

Per Planespotters.net, the Qatar Airways widebody fleet is much larger than its narrowbody fleet. The Middle Eastern carrier flies two families of Airbus widebodies: the A380 (eight jets) and the A350 (64 jets). The A350s are divided into 34 A350-900s and 30 A350-1000s. The airline also flies 93 777s (six 777-200s, 57 777-300ERs and 30 777Fs) and 61 Dreamliners (32 787-8s and 29 787-9s).

This distribution across four aircraft families produces a total widebody fleet for Qatar Airways of 226 planes. For comparison, the airline flies just 25 Airbus A320s and six A321s, totaling 31 narrowbody aircraft.

Brussels Airport will add eight manual border-control positions for arriving passengers by the end of 2026 and install six additional electronic gates in early 2027, as long waiting times linked to the European Entry/Exit System (EES) continue to disrupt passenger flows. The latest investment comes despite an earlier expansion of border-control infrastructure, with the airport saying that processing times under the new system remain significantly longer than anticipated. Brussels Airport is also pointing to unresolved technical problems affecting government-supplied registration equipment and calling for further action by European authorities.

The EES introduces digital registration of non-EU nationals travelling into and out of the Schengen Area, including the collection of facial images and fingerprints. According to Brussels Airport, the additional procedures have substantially increased the time required to process arriving passengers. During morning peak periods, the average processing time for each arriving visa passenger is now two to three times longer than before the system’s introduction. The airport says this has resulted in long queues at border control, with waiting times of two to four hours regularly reported at airports across Europe. After a slight improvement in August, waiting times at Brussels Airport increased again in September as biometric registration activity rose.

The airport had already increased the number of manual border-control positions by 20 per cent at arrivals and 25 per cent at departures during 2025, ahead of the EES rollout. These increases exceeded passenger traffic growth, but have proved insufficient to offset the longer processing times. The eight additional positions planned for December will increase arrival border-control capacity by 66 per cent, according to the airport. This means manual capacity at arrivals will have doubled within 12 months. The airport says the new positions must still be brought into operation in consultation with the authorities and other partners involved.

A further six electronic gates, ordered from the Federal Police in May 2026 and scheduled for delivery in early 2027, are expected to increase e-gate capacity at arrivals by 50 per cent. However, access to automated border checks remains restricted for some non-European travellers. Certain nationalities that could previously use e-gates are no longer eligible to do so under the new procedures, while other passengers must first complete EES registration.
Government registration technology still not operational

One of the more significant problems highlighted by Brussels Airport concerns 60 pre-registration kiosks purchased last year to help travellers complete EES registration before reaching a manual border-control desk. The kiosks were intended to reduce the workload at staffed counters and allow eligible non-EU nationals to use electronic gates.

Although the competent authorities decided before the summer that travellers from certain non-European countries could use the system, Brussels Airport says technical problems involving government suppliers mean the kiosks are still not operational. The airport expects the technology to help reduce queues, particularly for departing passengers, once it becomes available. On arrival, however, access to e-gates remains limited to certain nationalities and travellers already registered in the EES.

Brussels Airport is also calling for improvements to the implementation of the EES at European level, backing demands from Airports Council International Europe (ACI Europe) and Airlines for Europe. Proposed measures include optimising biometric checks and introducing a widely available application through which travellers could register in advance. Brussels Airport says only Sweden and Portugal currently offer such an application, and that a suitable solution should also be available in Belgium.

The airport further argues that authorities should retain sufficient flexibility to respond when queues become excessive. One measure it supports is the temporary suspension of biometric registration during periods of severe congestion, while maintaining the necessary security checks.

The expansion plans underline the operational challenge facing Brussels Airport as the EES becomes part of routine border processing. While additional counters and electronic gates should increase capacity, the airport’s own assessment indicates that infrastructure alone will not resolve the problem. The timely introduction of the delayed registration technology, wider access to automated checks and changes to the system’s implementation will also be necessary if waiting times are to return to acceptable levels.

Brussels Airport says it is working with the relevant authorities and government departments through a dedicated steering group, with the stated objective of maintaining secure and accurate border checks while reducing delays for passengers.

body_zh: 由于 EES 持续延误，布鲁塞尔机场扩大边境管制，政府登记亭仍处于离线状态 - Aviation24.be
首页 机场 布鲁塞尔机场 (BRU) 由于 EES 延误持续、政府登记，布鲁塞尔机场将扩大边境管制...
布鲁塞尔机场将在 2026 年底前为抵达旅客增加 8 个手动边境管制站，并在 2027 年初安装 6 个额外的电子登机口，因为与欧洲出入境系统 (EES) 相关的漫长等待时间继续扰乱客流。尽管早些时候扩大了边境管制基础设施，但最新的投资还是出现了，机场表示新系统下的处理时间仍然比预期长得多。布鲁塞尔机场还指出，尚未解决的技术问题影响了政府提供的登记设备，并呼吁欧洲当局采取进一步行动。
EES 引入了对进出申根区的非欧盟国民进行数字登记，包括收集面部图像和指纹。据布鲁塞尔机场称，额外的程序大大增加了处理抵达乘客所需的时间。在早高峰期间，每位入境签证旅客的平均处理时间比该系统推出前长了两到三倍。机场表示，这导致边境管制处排起长队，欧洲各地机场的等待时间经常长达两到四个小时。继 8 月份略有改善后，随着生物识别登记活动的增加，布鲁塞尔机场的等待时间在 9 月份再次增加。
在 EES 推出之前，机场已于 2025 年将抵达时的手动边境管制位置数量增加了 20%，出发时的手动边境管制位置数量增加了 25%。这些增长超过了客运量的增长，但事实证明不足以抵消更长的处理时间。据机场称，计划于 12 月增设 8 个职位，将使入境边境管制能力增加 66%。这意味着到达站的人工运力将在 12 个月内增加一倍。机场表示，新职位的投入运营仍必须与当局和其他相关合作伙伴协商。
联邦警察于 2026 年 5 月订购了另外 6 个电子登机口，计划于 2027 年初交付，预计将使电子登机口的入境容量增加 50%。然而，对于一些非欧洲旅客来说，进行自动边境检查仍然受到限制。根据新程序，以前可以使用电子登机口的某些国籍的乘客不再有资格使用，而其他乘客必须首先完成 EES 注册。
政府登记技术仍未投入使用
布鲁塞尔机场强调的更重要的问题之一涉及去年购买的 60 个预登记亭，以帮助旅客在到达手动边境管制柜台之前完成 EES 登记。这些信息亭的目的是减少柜台的工作量，并允许符合条件的非欧盟国民使用电子门。
尽管主管部门在今年夏天之前决定允许来自某些非欧洲国家的旅客使用该系统，但布鲁塞尔机场表示，涉及政府供应商的技术问题意味着这些自助值机亭仍无法运行。机场预计，一旦这项技术投入使用，将有助于减少排队现象，特别是对于离境旅客而言。然而，抵达后，电子登机口的使用仍然仅限于某些国籍和已在 EES 中注册的旅客。
布鲁塞尔机场还呼吁在欧洲层面改进 EES 的实施，支持欧洲国际机场理事会 (ACI Europe) 和欧洲航空公司的要求。拟议的措施包括优化生物识别检查并引入广泛使用的应用程序，旅客可以通过该应用程序提前登记。布鲁塞尔机场表示，目前只有瑞典和葡萄牙提供此类应用程序，比利时也应该有合适的解决方案。
机场进一步辩称，当局应保留足够的灵活性，以便在排队人数过多时做出反应。它支持的一项措施是在严重拥堵期间暂时停止生物识别注册，同时保持必要的安全检查。
随着 EES 成为常规边境处理的一部分，扩建计划凸显了布鲁塞尔机场面临的运营挑战。虽然额外的柜台和电子门应该会增加容量，但机场自己的评估表明，仅靠基础设施并不能解决问题。如果等待时间要恢复到可接受的水平，还需要及时引入延迟注册技术、更广泛地使用自动检查以及对系统实施进行更改。
布鲁塞尔机场表示，它正在通过一个专门的指导小组与有关当局和政府部门合作，其既定目标是维持安全和准确的边境检查，同时减少乘客的延误。

title_en: Allegiant orders six more Boeing 737 MAX jets for 2028 delivery

summary: Allegiant Air has ordered six additional Boeing 737 MAX aircraft for delivery in 2028, exercising its first purchase… The post Allegiant orders six more Boeing 737 MAX jets for 2028 delivery appeared first on AeroTime .
summary_zh: 忠诚航空已额外订购六架波音 737 MAX 飞机，将于 2028 年交付，这是其首次采购……忠诚航空订购了六架波音 737 MAX 飞机。
body_en: Allegiant Air has ordered six additional Boeing 737 MAX aircraft for delivery in 2028, exercising its first purchase options under an agreement signed with Boeing in 2021.

The Las Vegas-based airline disclosed the purchase on October 23, 2026. The six 737-8s bring its firm purchases under the agreement to 56 aircraft, of which 22 had been delivered as of October 23. Allegiant retains options for another 74 jets.
Allegiant listed the six aircraft’s combined list price at more than $720 million before discounts and price adjustments through delivery. It did not disclose the negotiated purchase price.

The order extends Allegiant’s investment in new Boeing aircraft after years of building its low-cost operation largely around used jets. When it announced the original 50-aircraft purchase in January 2022, Allegiant operated 108 Airbus A319s and A320s.

The original deal included the smaller 737-7 and higher-capacity 737-8-200, with options for 50 more aircraft. Allegiant said the new jets would allow it to replace retiring aircraft and expand its fleet while lowering fuel consumption.
Allegiant originally expected to receive its first MAX in 2023 and all 50 firm aircraft by the end of 2025, but deliveries were delayed. Its first 737-8-200 arrived in September 2024.

In November 2024, the airline amended its agreement with Boeing to reduce the number of aircraft arriving in 2024 and 2025 and extend deliveries of the original order through the end of 2027. Allegiant said that agreement also included benefits and other considerations related to the delays.

The first Allegiant MAX entered passenger service in October 2024. In an investor presentation that month, Allegiant said delivery delays were costing it approximately $30 million annually and that it was working with Boeing to seek compensation.

At the time of the original announcement, Allegiant said the MAX aircraft would burn approximately 20% less fuel than its older Airbus A320-family jets while offering more seats. The airline also signed a 12-year maintenance agreement with CFM International covering the new aircraft’s LEAP-1B engines.
The latest purchase leaves 34 firm aircraft still to be delivered under the Boeing agreement.
The post Allegiant orders six more Boeing 737 MAX jets for 2028 delivery appeared first on AeroTime .
body_zh: 忠实航空已额外订购了六架波音 737 MAX 飞机，将于 2028 年交付，根据 2021 年与波音公司签署的协议行使首次购买选择权。
这家总部位于拉斯维加斯的航空公司于 2026 年 10 月 23 日披露了此次采购事宜。这家 6 架 737-8 飞机将根据协议确定采购 56 架飞机，其中 22 架已于 10 月 23 日交付。Allegiant 保留另外 74 架喷气式飞机的选择权。
Allegiant 列出的六架飞机在折扣和交付价格调整前的总标价超过 7.2 亿美元。它没有透露协商的购买价格。
在多年来主要围绕二手飞机建立低成本运营之后，该订单扩大了忠诚公司对新型波音飞机的投资。当忠实于 2022 年 1 月宣布最初购买 50 架飞机时，运营着 108 架空客 A319 和 A320。
最初的交易包括较小的 737-7 和容量较大的 737-8-200，以及另外 50 架飞机的选择。 Allegiant 表示，新飞机将使其能够替换退役的飞机并扩大机队，同时降低燃油消耗。
Allegiant 最初预计于 2023 年接收第一架 MAX，并于 2025 年底接收全部 50 架飞机，但交付被推迟。首架 737-8-200 于 2024 年 9 月抵达。
2024 年 11 月，该航空公司修改了与波音公司的协议，减少了 2024 年和 2025 年抵达的飞机数量，并将原始订单的交付期限延长至 2027 年底。Allegiant 表示，该协议还包括与延误相关的好处和其他考虑因素。
第一架 Allegiant MAX 于 2024 年 10 月投入客运服务。在当月的投资者介绍中，Allegiant 表示，交付延误每年给该公司造成约 3000 万美元的损失，该公司正在与波音公司合作寻求赔偿。
在最初发布公告时，Allegiant 表示 MAX 飞机将比其旧款空客 A320 系列飞机燃烧约 20% 的燃油，同时提供更多座位。该航空公司还与 CFM International 签署了一份为期 12 年的维护协议，涵盖新飞机的 LEAP-1B 发动机。
根据波音协议，最新购买的飞机仍有 34 架飞机有待交付。
Allegiant 又订购了 6 架波音 737 MAX 喷气式飞机，将于 2028 年交付，这一消息首先出现在 AeroTime 上。

title_en: Qatar Airways Airbus A321LRs With Flat Bed Business Class Launching Soon
title_zh: 卡塔尔航空配备可平躺商务舱的空客 A321LR 即将推出
summary: Qatar Airways expects to take delivery of its first Airbus A321LR in the coming weeks, and we now know the 1-1 business class seat it will use.
summary_zh: 卡塔尔航空预计将在未来几周内接收第一架空客 A321LR，我们现在知道它将使用的 1-1 商务舱座椅。
body_en: In the coming months, Qatar Airways is expected to take delivery of its first Airbus A321LR, which will be the carrier’s first narrow body aircraft featuring latest generation interiors, including flat beds. We’ve known that the airline would introduce a “mini-Qsuite” type product, and we now have details of which seating platform the airline has selected.
Qatar Airways will take delivery of 10 Airbus A321LRs

Qatar Airways currently has a total of 50 factory fresh Airbus A321-family aircraft on order. This includes 10 A321LRs, and 40 A321neos — both of those are latest generation aircraft, with the A321LR featuring additional range.
The expectation is that the first A321LR will be delivered in the coming weeks, before the end of 2026. The 10 A321LRs should join the fleet pretty quickly, and will then be followed by the A321neos.

The A321LR has a maximum range of 4,000 nautical miles, so it can be used for many destinations in Europe, Africa, and Asia. Below is a map showing the rough range from Doha (though in reality it won’t be quite as far, accounting for winds, fuel reserves, etc.).

Now, for those paying close attention, I should acknowledge that Qatar Airways briefly flew six leased, all-economy A321neos , but those were just intended as a temporary solution, and are now flying for Sun PhuQuoc Airways, which is running an interesting operation .

Qatar Airways’ A321neo-family aircraft order goes back a long time, and involved a lot of drama. The order was first announced in 2011, then the airline reconfirmed and upsized it in 2017. However, then former Qatar Airways CEO Akbar Al Baker got into a fight with Airbus over A350 production quality, and refused to take delivery of any Airbus planes.

That turned into a massive court battle, which was eventually resolved . But in the process, Qatar Airways lost all of its Airbus delivery slots , which is why these planes are coming way later than initially expected .
Qatar Airways A321LRs get STELIA Aerospace OPERA seats

Qatar Airways has been promising all along that it would introduce some sort of a next generation flat bed business class product on its Airbus A321LRs. As you’d expect, business class seats on narrow bodies sometimes differ from those on wide bodies, due to differing cabin constraints.

So we now know which business class product Qatar Airways has selected for the A321LR. Executive Traveller quotes Qatar Airways CEO Hamad Ali Al-Khater as saying that the new business class product will be based on the STELIA Aerospace OPERA platform.

The expectation is that these planes will boast 16 business class seats, in a 1-1 configuration. This product offers reverse herringbone seats, and Qatar Airways plans to have doors at each seat as well, of course with its customized finishes.
The launch customer for the STELIA Aerospace OPERA platform was Air France on its A350s . However, that’s the wide body version of the seat, which is modified from the narrow body version.
When it comes to the narrow body version of the STELIA Aerospace OPERA platform, ITA Airways was the launch customer, on its A321neos .

This is also the product that Etihad is installing on its A321LRs . ITA Airways and Etihad don’t have doors in business class, but Qatar Airways does plan to offer it. Etihad also markets the first row of the cabin as first class (and that has doors), but I wouldn’t expect Qatar Airways to do something similar.
This is about as good as narrow body business class seats get, as it’s generally preferred to the herringbone seats you’ll find on other carriers, like JetBlue A321LRs , American A321XLRs , etc.

In the coming weeks, Qatar Airways is expected to take delivery of its first of 10 Airbus A321LRs. This will be the first custom designed next generation narrow body that the airline takes delivery of. We knew the airline would offer flat bed seats on these planes, and now we have the details of that.

The airline has gone with the STELIA Aerospace OPERA platform, the same product you’ll find on similar planes of Etihad and ITA Airways. However, unlike those airlines, Qatar Airways will have doors in business class.
What do you make of Qatar Airways’ upcoming A321LRs, and the planned interiors?
body_zh: 在未来几个月内，卡塔尔航空预计将接收其首架空客 A321LR，这将是该公司第一架采用最新一代内饰（包括平躺床）的窄体飞机。我们知道该航空公司将推出“​​mini-Qsuite”型产品，现在我们已经了解了该航空公司选择的座位平台的详细信息。
卡塔尔航空将接收 10 架空客 A321LR 飞机
卡塔尔航空目前总共订购了 50 架出厂新空客 A321 系列飞机。其中包括 10 架 A321LR 和 40 架 A321neo——这两架飞机都是最新一代飞机，其中 A321LR 具有更大的航程。
预计第一架 A321LR 将在未来几周内（即 2026 年底之前）交付。这 10 架 A321LR 应该很快就会加入机队，然后是 A321neo。
A321LR的最大航程为4000海里，因此可用于欧洲、非洲和亚洲的许多目的地。下面的地图显示了从多哈出发的大致范围（尽管考虑到风、燃料储备等因素，实际上不会那么远）。
现在，对于那些密切关注的人，我应该承认卡塔尔航空公司短暂地飞行了六架租赁的全经济型 A321neo，但这些只是作为临时解决方案，现在正在为 Sun PhuQuoc Airways 飞行，该航空公司正在进行一项有趣的运营。
卡塔尔航空的 A321neo 系列飞机订单可以追溯到很久以前，并且涉及很多戏剧性的事情。该订单于2011年首次宣布，随后于2017年再次确认并扩大了订单规模。然而，时任卡塔尔航空首席执行官阿克巴尔·阿尔·贝克(Akbar Al Baker)与空客就A350的生产质量发生争执，并拒绝接收任何空客飞机。
这变成了一场大规模的法庭斗争，最终得到了解决。但在此过程中，卡塔尔航空失去了所有空客的交付时段，这就是为什么这些飞机的抵达时间比最初预期要晚得多。
卡塔尔航空 A321LR 获得 STELIA Aerospace OPERA 座位
卡塔尔航空一直承诺将在其空客 A321LR 上推出某种下一代平板商务舱产品。正如您所料，由于客舱限制不同，窄体飞机的商务舱座椅有时与宽体飞机的商务舱座椅有所不同。
现在我们知道卡塔尔航空为 A321LR 选择了哪种商务舱产品。 Executive Traveler 援引卡塔尔航空首席执行官 Hamad Ali Al-Khater 的话说，新的商务舱产品将基于 STELIA Aerospace OPERA 平台。
预计这些飞机将拥有 16 个商务舱座位，采用 1-1 布局。该产品提供反向人字形座椅，卡塔尔航空还计划在每个座椅上安装门，当然还有定制的饰面。
STELIA Aerospace OPERA 平台的启动客户是法国航空 A350 飞机。不过，那是宽体版的座椅，是由窄体版改装而成的。
当谈到 STELIA Aerospace OPERA 平台的窄体版本时，ITA Airways 是 A321neos 的首发客户。
这也是阿提哈德航空在其 A321LR 上安装的产品。 ITA 航空和阿提哈德航空没有商务舱，但卡塔尔航空确实计划提供商务舱。阿提哈德还将第一排客舱定位为头等舱（并且有门），但我不认为卡塔尔航空会做类似的事情。
这与窄体商务舱座椅一样好，因为它通常比您在其他航空公司（如捷蓝 A321LR、美国 A321XLR 等）上找到的人字形座椅更受青睐。
在未来几周内，卡塔尔航空预计将接收其 10 架空客 A321LR 中的第一架。这将是该航空公司接收的第一架定制设计的下一代窄体飞机。我们知道航空公司会在这些飞机上提供平躺座椅，现在我们了解了详细信息。
该航空公司采用了 STELIA Aerospace OPERA 平台，您可以在阿提哈德航空和 ITA 航空的类似飞机上找到相同的产品。然而，与这些航空公司不同的是，卡塔尔航空将开设商务舱。
您如何看待卡塔尔航空即将推出的 A321LR 以及计划的内饰？

title_en: New Qatar Airways Qsuite Next Gen Business Class Launching Mid-2027, But Not As Planned
title_zh: 卡塔尔航空全新 Qsuite 下一代商务舱将于 2027 年中期推出，但未按计划推出
summary: Qatar Airways' Qsuite Next Gen business class has been delayed by 777X problems, so the airline now plans to debut it on the Airbus A350-1000 in mid-2027.
summary_zh: 卡塔尔航空的 Qsuite Next Gen 商务舱因 777X 问题而被推迟，因此该航空公司目前计划于 2 年中在空客 A350-1000 上首次推出该服务
body_en: In July 2024, Qatar Airways unveiled its newest business class product, which will be known as Qsuites Next Gen. While the initial plan was for this to be installed as of late 2025, that timeline didn’t stick, due to delivery delays with the Boeing 777X. There’s an update, as Qatar Airways now intends to debut this product on the Airbus A350, as of mid-2027. Let’s cover all the details.
Qatar Airways plans new business class product

Qatar Airways is known for its Qsuites business class . This is one of the world’s best business class experiences , between an excellent soft and hard product. Nearly 10 years after the product was introduced, it’s available on most long haul aircraft , but not all. Even though this continues to be one of the world’s most incredible business class experiences, that’s not stopping the airline from innovating.

Qatar Airways plans to introduce Qsuite Next Gen, its newest long haul business class experience. This product is evolutionary rather than revolutionary, which isn’t surprising, when you consider how good Qatar Airways’ product already is. However, the improvements are substantial, and I have to imagine that this will easily be the world’s overall best business class experience.

The Qsuite Next Gen business class cabin has the same general layout as the current product, which is to say that it’s in a staggered configuration, alternating between being forward and rear facing. However, there are some significant improvements, which will be especially great for those traveling together.
Here are some of the highlights of what’s changing:

A new movable 4K OLED Panasonic Astrova inflight entertainment screen, which can be repositioned to the side to create the largest social and productivity space in the sky, for up to four passengers in the Quad Suite, and up to two passengers in the Companion Suite
New customization options, including ambient lighting, privacy controls, and a touchscreen passenger control unit
A larger lie flat seat, as well as a large double bed
Added privacy, with taller, digitally controlled dividers
New storage, including enclosed drawers where you can store your phone, watch, jewelry, etc.
Significantly improved tech, including new wireless charging
Below you can see a video and some pictures highlighting some of the features of the new Qsuite Next Gen experience.
With more space, personalization and comfort than ever before.
Welcome to Qsuite Next Gen. Luxury redefined. #QatarAirways #WorldsBestAirline pic.twitter.com/EawbsNji4o
— Qatar Airways (@qatarairways) July 22, 2024
Qatar Airways Qsuite Next Gen rollout schedule

Initially, Qatar Airways’ plan was to introduce the Qsuite Next Gen business class product on the Boeing 777-9. The airline has at least 60 of these planes on order , and when the product was unveiled mid-2024, the plan was for deliveries to start as of late 2025.

As you’d expect, that timeline has been pushed back considerably, as the 777X still isn’t certified . Currently, Qatar Airways expects to take delivery of its first 777X in late 2027, best case scenario… and that could easily be delayed again! We should also see a new first class product debut on these planes (or at least a subfleet of them).

However, with the continued 777X delays, the airline is developing a new plan. Executive Traveller quotes Qatar Airways CEO Hamad Ali Al-Khater as saying that Qsuite Next Gen will now debut in mid-2027, on the Airbus A350-1000. Specifically, the plan is that the remaining (roughly one dozen) A350 deliveries will feature these new cabins as of then.
body_zh: 2024 年 7 月，卡塔尔航空推出了其最新的商务舱产品，该产品将被称为 Qsuites Next Gen。虽然最初计划是在 2025 年末安装该产品，但由于波音 777X 的交付延迟，该时间表并未遵守。有一个更新，卡塔尔航空现在打算从 2027 年中期开始在空客 A350 上首次推出该产品。 Let’s cover all the details.
卡塔尔航空计划推出新的商务舱产品
卡塔尔航空以其 Qsuites 商务舱而闻名。这是世界上最好的商务舱体验之一，介于卓越的软硬产品之间。该产品推出近 10 年后，大多数长途飞机都配备了该产品，但并非全部。尽管这仍然是世界上最令人难以置信的商务舱体验之一，但这并没有阻止航空公司的创新。
卡塔尔航空计划推出 Qsuite Next Gen，这是其最新的长途商务舱体验。该产品是渐进式的，而不是革命性的，当你考虑到卡塔尔航空的产品已经有多好时，这并不奇怪。然而，改进是巨大的，我不得不想象这将很容易成为世界上整体上最好的商务舱体验。
Qsuite Next Gen商务舱的总体布局与现有产品相同，也就是说，它采用交错配置，前向和后向交替。然而，有一些重大改进，这对于一起旅行的人来说尤其有用。
以下是一些变化的亮点：
全新可移动 4K OLED 松下 Astrova 机上娱乐屏幕，可重新定位到侧面，打造空中最大的社交和生产力空间，四人套房中最多可容纳 4 名乘客，伴侣套房中最多可容纳 2 名乘客
新的定制选项，包括环境照明、隐私控制和触摸屏乘客控制单元
更大的平躺座椅以及一张大双人床
通过更高的数字控制隔板增加隐私
新的存储空间，包括封闭式抽屉，您可以在其中存放手机、手表、珠宝等。
显着改进的技术，包括新的无线充电
您可以在下面看到一段视频和一些图片，其中重点介绍了新的 Qsuite Next Gen 体验的一些功能。
拥有比以往更多的空间、个性化和舒适度。
欢迎来到 Qsuite Next Gen，重新定义奢华。 #QatarAirways #WorldsBestAirline pic.twitter.com/EawbsNji4o
— 卡塔尔航空 (@qatarairways) 2024 年 7 月 22 日
卡塔尔航空 Qsuite Next Gen 推出时间表
最初，卡塔尔航空的计划是在波音 777-9 上推出 Qsuite Next Gen 商务舱产品。该航空公司至少订购了 60 架此类飞机，该产品于 2024 年中期推出时，计划于 2025 年末开始交付。
正如您所料，由于 777X 仍未获得认证，该时间表已被大幅推迟。目前，卡塔尔航空预计将在 2027 年底接收其首架 777X，这是最好的情况……而这很容易再次推迟！我们还应该看到新的头等舱产品在这些飞机（或至少其中的一个子机队）上首次亮相。
然而，随着 777X 的持续延误，该航空公司正在制定新计划。 Executive Traveler 援引卡塔尔航空首席执行官 Hamad Ali Al-Khater 的话说，Qsuite Next Gen 将于 2027 年中期在空客 A350-1000 上首次亮相。具体来说，计划是剩余的（大约十几架）A350 交付将配备这些新客舱。

title_en: American Flight Returns To Miami Over Water Request Dispute (Guyana’s President Was Onboard)
title_zh: 美国航班因用水请求纠纷返回迈阿密（圭亚那总统在机上）
summary: An American Airlines flight from Miami to Guyana turned back shortly after takeoff when a passenger reportedly threatened a flight attendant over a water request. Guyana's president was onboard.
summary_zh: 美国航空一架从迈阿密飞往圭亚那的航班起飞后不久就返航，据报道一名乘客因与一名空乘人员发生冲突而威胁空乘人员。
body_en: An American Airlines flight had to return to its origin shortly after takeoff, after a passenger was accused of threatening the crew during a dispute arising from a request for water. Perhaps what makes this story even more interesting is that the president of Guyana was reportedly onboard.
American flight diverts over “deal with him” threat to crew

This incident happened on Thursday, October 22, 2026, and involves American flight AA339 , operating from Miami (MIA) to Georgetown, Guyana (GEO). The 1,969-mile flight was operated by a Boeing 737 MAX 8, and took off at 6:40PM, roughly on schedule.

However, the plane didn’t make it far. Just 10 minutes after takeoff, while climbing through 22,000 feet, the decision was made to return to Miami. The plane ended up landing back in Miami at 7:18PM, 38 minutes after it first departed.
What was the reason for the return to the origin? According to a radio transmission from the pilots to air traffic control, the issue was a problem passenger:

“While we were climbing out, he rushed the flight attendants in the back of the aircraft. I guess the exact words were, ‘I will take care of you when we land in Guyana,’ but in a very threatening manner.”

According to passengers onboard, what happened is that a passenger got up while the seatbelt sign was still on during the climb, and attempted to help himself to a bottle of water, for a relative who was having a panic attack.

The passenger was reportedly told to return to his seat by a flight attendant, and the two got into a verbal confrontation, which is when the passenger told the flight attendant that he would “deal with” him when they reach Guyana.
The flight attendant took that statement as a threat, and informed the pilots, who made the decision to return to Miami.

The Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office was called to meet the plane, based on an initial report of a flight attendant being assaulted by a passenger. However, according to a statement, “the investigation revealed the passenger and flight attendant were involved in a verbal dispute and no assault was committed.”

The passenger ended up being removed from the plane and the police interviewed passengers. There was then a crew change, and the plane eventually took off at 10:42PM and landed in Guyana at 2:55AM, over four hours behind schedule.
The president of Guyana happened to be on this flight

This is more a funny coincidence than anything else, but the president of Guyana, Irfaan Ali, happened to be on this flight . It looks like he had been in the US to establish an enhanced military partnership with the United States, and had met with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth the day prior.
So he was inconvenienced by this just like everyone else. I don’t imagine that his presence had anything to do with the decision to divert.

I wasn’t there, so I can’t really speak as to how threatening this entire situation was. Based on what we know, it sure sounds like there may have been a lack of deescalation skills, and that this was more about bruised egos than anything.

Of course you shouldn’t get up when a plane is ascending and suggest you’ll “deal with” flight attendant when you land. Flight attendants shouldn’t have to tolerate that. At the same time, I can’t imagine that this passenger actually posed any sort of a threat to the flight, and instead, it was likely just trash talking.

An American flight scheduled to operate from Miami to Guyana returned to its origin after a passenger became threatening with a flight attendant. While the plane was climbing out, a traveler reportedly went to the rear galley to get water, and ended up getting into a confrontation with a flight attendant, claiming he would “deal with” him once he got to Guyana.

The crew asked authorities to meet the plane, and claimed that a flight attendant was assaulted. However, the police reported it was just a verbal confrontation, and no charges were filed. The interesting twist in all of this is that the president of Guyana was also onboard the flight.
What do you make of this American diversion to Miami?
body_zh: 美国航空的一架航班在起飞后不久不得不返回出发地，原因是一名乘客被指控在因要求喝水而引发的纠纷中威胁机组人员。也许让这个故事更有趣的是据报道圭亚那总统也在船上。
美国航班因机组人员“对付他”威胁而改道
该事件发生于 2026 年 10 月 22 日星期四，涉及从迈阿密 (MIA) 飞往圭亚那乔治敦 (GEO) 的美国航空 AA339 航班。这趟航程 1,969 英里的航班由波音 737 MAX 8 运营，于下午 6:40 起飞，大致按计划起飞。
然而，飞机并没有飞多远。起飞后仅 10 分钟，在爬升 22,000 英尺的高度时，我们决定返回迈阿密。飞机最终于晚上 7 点 18 分返回迈阿密，即起飞 38 分钟后。
回到原点的原因是什么？根据飞行员向空中交通管制中心的无线电传输，问题出在一名有问题的乘客身上：
“当我们爬出来时，他冲了飞机后部的空乘人员。我猜确切的话语是，‘当我们降落在圭亚那时，我会照顾你们’，但语气非常具有威胁性。”
据机上乘客称，当时的情况是，一名乘客在爬升过程中，在安全带指示灯还亮着的情况下起身，试图为惊恐发作的亲戚取一瓶水。
据报道，一名空乘人员让该乘客返回座位，两人发生了言语冲突，当时该乘客告诉空乘人员，当他们到达圭亚那时，他会“处理”他。
空乘人员将此言论视为威胁，并通知了飞行员，飞行员决定返回迈阿密。
根据空乘人员遭到乘客袭击的初步报告，迈阿密戴德县治安官办公室被叫去接机。然而，根据一份声明，“调查显示，乘客和空乘人员发生了言语争执，并未发生殴打行为。”
该乘客最终被带下飞机，警方对乘客进行了询问。随后机组人员进行了换班，飞机最终于晚上 10:42 起飞，并于凌晨 2:55 降落在圭亚那，比原计划晚了四个多小时。
圭亚那总统恰好乘坐这趟航班
这比什么都更有趣的巧合，但圭亚那总统伊尔法安·阿里恰好在这架航班上。看来他来美国是为了与美国建立加强的军事伙伴关系，并在前一天会见了战争部长皮特·赫格斯。
所以他和其他人一样，也因此受到了不便。我不认为他的存在与转移的决定有任何关系。
我当时不在现场，所以我无法真正说出整个情况的威胁有多大。根据我们所知，听起来肯定是缺乏降级技能，这更多的是自尊心受伤而不是任何事情。
当然，你不应该在飞机上升时站起来并建议你在着陆时“对付”空乘人员。空乘人员不应该容忍这种情况。同时，我无法想象这位乘客实际上对航班构成了任何形式的威胁，相反，这很可能只是垃圾话。
一架计划从迈阿密飞往圭亚那的美国航班在一名乘客威胁空乘人员后返回出发地。据报道，当飞机爬出时，一名旅客去后厨房取水，最终与一名空乘人员发生冲突，声称一旦他到达圭亚那就会“处理”他。
机组人员要求当局与飞机会面，并声称一名空乘人员遭到袭击。不过，警方表示这只是言语冲突，并未提出任何指控。所有这一切中有趣的转折是圭亚那总统也在飞机上。

title_en: What SR-71 Blackbird Pilots Had To Do Before Missions That Most Other Pilots In History Have Never Done
title_zh: SR-71 黑鸟飞行员在执行历史上大多数其他飞行员从未执行过的任务之前必须做什么
summary: The SR-71 was one of the most extreme airplanes ever built and forced pilots to often train and prepare more like astronauts than typical pilots.
summary_zh: SR-71 是有史以来制造的最极端的飞机之一，迫使飞行员经常像宇航员一样进行训练和准备，而不是典型的飞行员。
body_en: What SR-71 Blackbird Pilots Had To Do Before Missions That Most Other Pilots In History Have Never Done

Aaron is an aviation enthusiast and world traveler with a deep interest in aerospace history and technology. He has traveled around the world numerous times, often incorporating visits to aviation museums and historic aircraft collections into his journeys. A native of New Zealand, he is an expert in aviation and maintains a broad interest in a variety of other subjects.

The Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird was not a normal aircraft . It was the fastest air-breathing aircraft ever made and was designed to fly at such a height (over 80,000 feet or around 24,300 meters) and speed (over Mach 3) that it could outpace enemy air defense and missiles. There are confirmed reports that it successfully outflew around 4,000 missiles fired at it over the course of its career.

The aircraft was built to fly higher and faster than the subsonic Lockheed U-2 spy plane that had proven itself vulnerable to enemy air defense since 1960. The SR-71 was designed so that the United States could gather intelligence throughout the Soviet Union and other countries of interest. This was a time before satellites, the internet, and the USSR had largely closed its borders to foreigners.

Before the Lockheed U-2, the US was left largely guessing what was happening in the USSR. The value of these spy planes was displayed in 1962 when a U-2 discovered Soviet missiles in Cuba, triggering the Cuban Missile Crisis, while also highlighting the vulnerability, as a U-2 was the only aircraft successfully intercepted. The successor SR-71 was more extreme than the U-2 and pushed pilots to cross over with astronauts.

While the Lockheed SR-71 was an air-breathing aircraft that flew in the atmosphere, it was so extreme that its crews had to go through procedures that had more in common with astronauts than with typical pilots. Blackbird crews had to wear full-pressure full-body suites derived from those used by astronauts . Before flight, pilots had to undergo lengthy suit-fitting procedures while also checking for leaks and inspecting the oxygen systems.

Technicians were required to step into the rear-entry suit like 'a new skin.' They needed to adjust layers, including the comfort liner, the bladder/thermal layer, and the restraint layer. The pilots had to don the parachute harness, boots, a completely sealed helmet, and gloves. The boots even came with spurs for egress. Every seal, zipper, and hose of the David Clark S1030 full-pressure suit had to be meticulously checked.

The suit was heavy, restrictive, and relied on a portable cooling unit that the pilots carried with them to the aircraft to keep from overheating before the SR-71's cockpit air conditioning could kick in. The Flight Test Historical Museum says of the suit that " the S1030 evolved from its remote ancestor, the original David Clark XMC-2-DC suit first produced in 1956, via the Pilot’s Protective Assembly (PPA) model S901 worn by the first SR-71 crews ."

A released CIA report said that " crew preparations for the AVIATION 'WEEK demonstration flight began more than three hours before the flight with a high-protein breakfast of steak and eggs . " It went on to explain that the Air Force's Physiological Support Division maintained dedicated dining facilities specifically for SR-71 and U-2 Dragon Lady crews. Around an hour and a half before takeoff, the crews would undergo medical checks, including temperature, blood pressure, and general physical condition.

The high-protein preparatory diet was the strike's operational requirement . The crew needed to have a high-protein, 'low-residue' meal that could be entirely absorbed by the body and therefore minimize the need for bowel movements. Once in the suits and zooming at 85,000 feet (25,900 meters), the pilot's flight suits didn't accommodate bathroom breaks. A gastrointestinal issue in that pressurized space suit could ruin a mission or worse.

With that said, the pilots sometimes wore a urine collection device that had a tube that attached to a manually operated valve on the inside of the left leg. The meal also allowed the pilots to sustain energy on long missions, although their meal could sometimes be supplemented later on with tube foods like applesauce in the helmet.
Emergency squawks, holds, NOTAMs — live signals, no signup.
Emergency squawks, holds, NOTAMs — live signals, no signup.

Related to fitting the astronaut-like suit was breathing pure oxygen before takeoff. In order to prevent decompression sickness (aka the bends), crews had to breathe 100% oxygen for around an hour before the flight. This allowed nitrogen to be purged from their bloodstream. Some sources say the pre-breathing period would last at least 30 minutes.

Once the aircraft was flying at altitude, a sudden depressurization would expose the crew to conditions close to space and would help stave off decompression sickness; no human can survive in those conditions for long. The aircraft was designed so that the pilots could bail out and eject at 85,000 feet. Although doing so at that altitude and at around three times the speed of sound was extremely risky and required a very specific and carefully engineered sequence. This practice continues today for astronauts
Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird Stats (Per the Air Force Museum )

In 2024, NASA said that during the Exploration Atmosphere Prebreathe Protocol Study , eight crew members spent 11 days in a reduced-pressure, 20-foot chamber at NASA’s Johnson Space Center. This would determine how spacewalk operations can be conducted safely and frequently on the surface of the Moon or Mars. NASA added that " the study evaluates alternative prebreathe protocols for crewmembers, maximizing time on spacewalks while minimizing risk of decompression sickness for the astronauts ."

Even getting into the aircraft before the flight was an extensive procedure. Before the pressure suits were hot and uncomfortable, the crews were transported in a van equipped with cooling hoses. Even after they got into the cockpit, the cooling support remained essential. SR-71 crews could normally try to be in the aircraft 50–55 minutes before the scheduled takeoff. The engines were started around 40 minutes prior to takeoff.

Long before the crew had arrived at the aircraft, the maintenance personnel had spent hours checking the aircraft's crew survival equipment, cabin pressurization, and environmental control systems. While it is often well known that fires were lit under trucks to allow them to start in Second World War winters (such as in the Soviet Union), the fact that the SR-71's oil was unusually thick and needed to be pre-heated for the engines to start is less well-known.
body_zh: SR-71 黑鸟飞行员在执行历史上大多数其他飞行员从未执行过的任务之前必须做什么
亚伦是一位航空爱好者和环球旅行家，对航空航天历史和技术有着浓厚的兴趣。他曾多次环游世界，经常在旅途中参观航空博物馆和历史飞机收藏。他是新西兰人，是航空专家，并对其他各种学科保持着广泛的兴趣。
洛克希德 SR-71 黑鸟不是一架普通的飞机。它是有史以来速度最快的吸气式飞机，其设计飞行高度（超过 80,000 英尺或约 24,300 米）和速度（超过 3 马赫）足以超越敌方防空系统和导弹。有证实的报道称，它在其服役生涯中成功击退了约 4,000 枚向其发射的导弹。
该飞机的设计目标是比亚音速洛克希德 U-2 间谍机飞得更高、更快，而自 1960 年以来，洛克希德 U-2 间谍机就已经证明自己很容易受到敌方防空系统的攻击。SR-71 的设计目的是让美国能够在整个苏联和其他感兴趣的国家收集情报。那是卫星、互联网和苏联基本上对外国人关闭边境之前的时代。

Before the Lockheed U-2, the US was left largely guessing what was happening in the USSR. 1962年，一架U-2在古巴发现了苏联导弹，引发了古巴导弹危机，同时也凸显了这些间谍机的脆弱性，因为U-2是唯一成功拦截的飞机。 The successor SR-71 was more extreme than the U-2 and pushed pilots to cross over with astronauts.
虽然洛克希德 SR-71 是一架在大气层中飞行的吸气式飞机，但它的工作环境非常极端，以至于其机组人员必须执行与宇航员比典型飞行员更相似的程序。黑鸟号机组人员必须穿着源自宇航员所用的全压全身套装。在飞行之前，飞行员必须经过漫长的西装试穿程序，同时还要检查泄漏情况并检查氧气系统。
技术人员被要求像“换上新皮肤”一样穿上后入式套装。他们需要调整各层，包括舒适衬里、膀胱/保暖层和约束层。飞行员必须穿戴降落伞安全带、靴子、完全密封的头盔和手套。靴子甚至还带有用于出口的马刺。 David Clark S1030 全压服的每个密封件、拉链和软管都必须经过仔细检查。
该套装笨重、限制性大，并且依赖于飞行员随身携带到飞机上的便携式冷却装置，以防止在 SR-71 驾驶舱空调启动之前过热。飞行测试历史博物馆在谈到该套装时表示，“S1030 是从它的远祖，即 1956 年首次生产的原始大卫·克拉克 XMC-2-DC 套装，通过第一名飞行员所穿的飞行员保护组件 (PPA) 型号 S901 演变而来的。 SR-71 机组人员。”
中央情报局发布的一份报告称，“机组人员在飞行前三个多小时就开始为‘航空周’示范飞行做准备，包括牛排和鸡蛋等高蛋白早餐。”报告接着解释说，空军生理支持部门专门为 SR-71 和 U-2 Dragon Lady 机组人员保留了专用餐饮设施。起飞前一个半小时左右，机组人员将接受体检，包括体温、血压和一般身体状况。
高蛋白准备饮食是罢工的作战要求。船员们需要高蛋白、“低残留”的膳食，可以完全被身体吸收，从而最大限度地减少排便的需要。穿上飞行服并在 85,000 英尺（25,900 米）的高度飞行后，飞行员的飞行服就无法容纳上厕所的时间。加压太空服中的肠胃问题可能会毁掉一次任务，甚至更糟。
话虽如此，飞行员有时会佩戴尿液收集装置，该装置有一根管子连接到左腿内侧的手动操作阀上。这种膳食还使飞行员能够在长途任务中保持能量，尽管他们的膳食有时可以在以后用头盔中的苹果酱等管状食物进行补充。
紧急呼叫、等待、航行通告 — 实时信号，无需注册。

与穿上类似宇航员的服装相关的是起飞前呼吸纯氧。为了防止减压病（又称减压病），机组人员必须在飞行前约一个小时呼吸 100% 的氧气。这使得氮气从他们的血液中被清除。有消息称，预呼吸期将持续至少 30 分钟。
一旦飞机在高空飞行，突然减压将使机组人员暴露在接近太空的条件下，有助于避免减压病；没有人能够在这种条件下长期生存。该飞机的设计使得飞行员可以在 85,000 英尺的高度跳伞和弹射。尽管在那个高度和大约三倍音速的情况下这样做是极其危险的，并且需要一个非常具体和精心设计的序列。宇航员的这种做法至今仍在继续
洛克希德 SR-71 黑鸟统计数据（根据空军博物馆）
2024 年，NASA 表示，在探索大气预呼吸协议研究期间，8 名机组人员在 NASA 约翰逊航天中心的一个 20 英尺减压室中度过了 11 天。这将决定如何在月球或火星表面安全、频繁地进行太空行走操作。美国宇航局补充说，“这项研究评估了宇航员的替代预呼吸方案，最大限度地延长太空行走时间，同时最大限度地减少宇航员患减压病的风险。”
即使在飞行前进入飞机也是一个繁琐的程序。在压力服变得又热又不舒服之前，工作人员是乘坐一辆配备冷却软管的货车运送的。即使他们进入驾驶舱后，冷却支持仍然至关重要。 SR-71 机组人员通常可以在预定起飞前 50-55 分钟尝试进入飞机。发动机在起飞前 40 分钟左右启动。
早在机组人员到达飞机之前，维护人员就花了几个小时检查飞机的机组救生设备、机舱增压和环境控制系统。虽然众所周知，在第二次世界大战的冬天（例如在苏联），卡车下方会生火以使其启动，但 SR-71 的油异常稠并且需要预热才能启动发动机这一事实却鲜为人知。

title_en: The 50-Seat Jet With A First Class Cabin United Airlines Is Using To Rebuild Its Newark Hub Feed
title_zh: 联合航空公司使用 50 座的头等舱喷气式飞机重建其纽瓦克枢纽航线
summary: United is aiming to bring feeder traffic back to Newark by using a first class cabin on a regional jet. What does this actually mean for passengers?
summary_zh: 美联航的目标是通过使用支线飞机上的头等舱将支线交通带回纽瓦克。这对乘客来说实际上意味着什么？
body_en: The 50-Seat Jet With A First Class Cabin United Airlines Is Using To Rebuild Its Newark Hub Feed
Airline and Airport Management Graduate, Student Commercial Pilot and Commercial Aviation Writer.

Traditionally, thin secondary markets need austere, high-density turboprops or cramped single-class jets to keep operating costs manageable. Legacy carriers routinely scale back mainline service to smaller cities, substituting minimalist cabin layouts where comfort is sacrificed for seat count. United Airlines has ignored this convention entirely by deploying a premium-heavy regional fleet to bolster its latest domestic network expansion.

Pairing GoJet's three-class Bombardier CRJ550 with Republic Airways' Embraer E175 aircraft totally reshapes connection potential at Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR). What United is able to show is that using regional aircraft can still bring in high-yield premium revenue even though the seat count is substantially lower than other popular jets. In addition, this strategy can keep premium revenue high without impacting the mainline fleet.

United Airlines launched four domestic routes from EWR on September 24, 2026, establishing direct links to Charlottesville, Virginia (CHO), Knoxville, Tennessee (TYS), Northwest Arkansas National Airport serving Bentonville, Arkansas (XNA), and Omaha, Nebraska (OMA), as per AeroRoutes . The expansion targets regional cities that lost direct service during pandemic-era contractions or long-term capacity realignments. Omaha and Knoxville services were suspended in 2020, and Bentonville's direct link went dark in 2022, leaving corporate and leisure travelers with cumbersome multi-stop itineraries.

Historical continuity varies across these restored city pairs, particularly for Charlottesville, where previous Newark operations dated back to Continental's schedule in 1997 or subsequent United Express frequencies ending in 2012, as noted in Simple Flying analysis . Network planners designed these flights to re-establish vital spoke connections into the New York metropolitan area, so that regional economies regain direct access to an international hub. Rather than launching unproven speculative markets, the airline chose to reactivate established demand pools backed by steady regional business and tourism.

Operational frequencies reflect varied demand density across these restored markets. Knoxville (TYS) received twice-daily service to accommodate heavy regional travel demand, while Charlottesville, Northwest Arkansas, and Omaha each operate on a once-daily schedule, establishing reliable baseline frequencies across each corridor.

Operating short regional hops with mainline-level passenger comfort meant deploying a specific aircraft type: the CRJ550 operated by regional partner GoJet Airlines. Unlike standard regional jets that force passengers to gate-check rolling luggage due to cramped overhead compartments, the CRJ550 is engineered around a spacious 50-seat cabin layout that provides dedicated overhead bin capacity for every traveler.

According to United Airlines seat maps , the three-class configuration includes a genuine first-class cabin featuring 10 seats, Economy Plus seating offering 34 inches to 36 inches (86.4 centimeters to 91.4 centimeters) of pitch, and standard economy rows, all packed into an airframe designed to bypass strict pilot union scope clauses limiting regional seating capacity to 50 seats . Passengers in the premium cabin have access to a self-serve refreshment center and upgraded seat width dimensions measuring 19.75 inches to 20 inches (50.2 centimeters to 50.8 centimeters) that mirror narrowbody mainline standards. This design philosophy gives corporate travelers on routes like Newark to Charlottesville or Knoxville an elevated onboard experience without needing a large mainline aircraft on low-volume sectors.

Deploying a low-capacity, high-amenity aircraft on thinner routes completely changes passenger perception of regional flying. Travelers accustomed to regional turboprops or cramped regional jets experience consistent product standards that align seamlessly with United's domestic and international fleet.

Thin markets like Charlottesville are served by the highly specialized CRJ550, but higher-density corporate and commercial corridors need a slightly larger regional platform to satisfy passenger volume. United paired GoJet operations with Republic Airways, bringing in the 76-seat E175 aircraft to handle daily rotations to Northwest Arkansas and Omaha.

The E175 provides an effective capacity step-up for markets driven by major corporate headquarters and agricultural trade. Northwest Arkansas serves as the main commercial gateway for Walmart and its extensive vendor network, demanding consistent multi-class seating capacity to accommodate corporate executives traveling to eastern financial centers. Similarly, Omaha generates robust business and agricultural demand that easily fills up a 76-seat regional cabin.

Integrating both the 50-seat CRJ550 and the 76-seat E175 allows United Express to fine-tune capacity deployment across its eastern seaboard hub. Fleet harmonization across regional partners helps ground handlers and flight crews to manage standardized equipment types efficiently within congested terminal environments.

Strategic scheduling of these four regional arrivals serves a singular purpose. The goal is to feed United's heavy bank of afternoon and evening international departures at EWR, so that load factors remain high across all potential connecting flights. Network schedulers structured flight times to land aircraft during midday connection banks, funneling regional passengers directly into widebody departures heading across the Atlantic to Europe and south toward Latin America.

Flight UA4414 from Charlottesville arrives at Newark at 2:12 PM, according to Deeparrival , providing sufficient cushion for travelers to connect smoothly onto transatlantic banking waves without enduring excessive terminal layovers. Overall, the hub-and-spoke mechanism used here makes regional flights less like standalone point-to-point loss-leaders, instead becoming far more vital revenue generators that support high-yielding long-haul routes.

This precision hub feed leaves zero room for schedule slippage, mainly because these regional arrivals are tightly synchronized with afternoon widebody departures. As a result, a single delayed inbound rotation from Charlottesville or Knoxville threatens to sever high-yield connections. Newark's hub control center maintains constant oversight of these arrival streams, deploying tactical mitigation strategies when air traffic control constraints or localized congestion threaten the integrity of the banking wave.
body_zh: 联合航空公司使用 50 座的头等舱喷气式飞机重建其纽瓦克枢纽航线
航空公司和机场管理毕业生、商业飞行员学生和商业航空作家。
传统上，规模较小的二级市场需要简朴、高密度的涡轮螺旋桨飞机或狭窄的单级喷气式飞机，以保持运营成本可控。传统航空公司通常会缩减飞往较小城市的干线服务，取而代之的是简约的客舱布局，为了座位数量而牺牲舒适度。美国联合航空公司完全无视这一惯例，部署了一支高端支线机队来支持其最新的国内网络扩张。
GoJet 的三舱庞巴迪 CRJ550 与共和航空的巴西航空工业公司 E175 飞机配对，彻底重塑了纽瓦克自由国际机场 (EWR) 的连接潜力。美联航能够证明的是，尽管支线飞机的座位数远低于其他受欢迎的喷气式飞机，但使用支线飞机仍然可以带来高收益的溢价收入。此外，这一策略可以在不影响干线机队的情况下保持较高的保费收入。

根据 AeroRoutes 的数据，联合航空于 2026 年 9 月 24 日开通了从 EWR 出发的 4 条国内航线，建立了直达弗吉尼亚州夏洛茨维尔 (CHO)、田纳西州诺克斯维尔 (TYS)、阿肯色州西北部国家机场的航线，为阿肯色州本顿维尔 (XNA) 和内布拉斯加州奥马哈 (OMA) 提供服务。此次扩张针对的是在大流行时期的经济收缩或长期运力调整期间失去直接服务的地区城市。奥马哈和诺克斯维尔的服务于 2020 年暂停，本顿维尔的直达航班于 2022 年关闭，给企业和休闲旅客留下了繁琐的多站行程。

这些恢复的城市对之间的历史连续性各不相同，特别是对于夏洛茨维尔，纽瓦克之前的运营可以追溯到 1997 年大陆航空的航班时刻表或随后于 2012 年结束的联合快运航班频率，如 Simple Flying 分析中所述。网络规划者设计这些航班的目的是重新建立与纽约大都市区的重要辐射连接，以便区域经济体重新获得与国际枢纽的直接联系。该航空公司没有启动未经证实的投机市场，而是选择重新激活由稳定的区域业务和旅游业支持的既定需求池。
运营频率反映了这些恢复市场的不同需求密度。诺克斯维尔 (TYS) 每天提供两班服务，以满足繁忙的区域旅行需求，而夏洛茨维尔、阿肯色州西北部和奥马哈则各自按每天一班的时间表运营，从而在每个走廊上建立了可靠的基线频率。
运营短途区域航班并提供干线级别的乘客舒适度意味着需要部署特定的飞机类型：由区域合作伙伴 GoJet 航空公司运营的 CRJ550。标准支线飞机因头顶行李舱狭窄而迫使乘客通过登机口检查滚动行李，而 CRJ550 则不同，CRJ550 的设计围绕宽敞的 50 座客舱布局进行设计，可为每位旅客提供专用的头顶行李箱容量。

根据联合航空的座位图，三舱配置包括真正的头等舱，设有 10 个座位，经济舱座位间距为 34 英寸至 36 英寸（86.4 厘米至 91.4 厘米），以及标准经济排，所有这些都装在一个机身中，旨在绕过严格的飞行员工会范围条款，将区域座位容量限制为 50 个座位。高级客舱的乘客可以使用自助茶点中心，座椅宽度尺寸升级为 19.75 英寸至 20 英寸（50.2 厘米至 50.8 厘米），符合窄体干线标准。这种设计理念为乘坐纽瓦克至夏洛茨维尔或诺克斯维尔等航线的商务旅客提供了更高的机上体验，而无需在低运量航段使用大型干线飞机。
在狭窄的航线上部署低载客量、高舒适度的飞机彻底改变了乘客对支线飞行的看法。习惯乘坐支线涡轮螺旋桨飞机或狭窄支线飞机的旅客可体验到与美联航国内和国际机队无缝对接的一致产品标准。
像夏洛茨维尔这样的人口稀少的市场由高度专业化的 CRJ550 提供服务，但密度较高的企业和商业走廊需要稍大的区域平台来满足乘客量。美联航将 GoJet 运营与共和航空配对，引入 76 座 E175 飞机来处理飞往阿肯色州西北部和奥马哈的日常航班。
E175 为主要公司总部和农产品贸易驱动的市场提供了有效的产能提升。阿肯色州西北部是沃尔玛及其广泛供应商网络的主要商业门户，需要一致的多舱位座位容量，以容纳前往东部金融中心的企业高管。同样，奥马哈产生了强劲的商业和农业需求，很容易就能填满 76 个座位的区域客舱。
通过整合 50 座 CRJ550 和 76 座 E175，联合快运能够微调其东部沿海枢纽的运力部署。区域合作伙伴之间的机队协调有助于地勤人员和机组人员在拥挤的航站楼环境中有效管理标准化设备类型。
对这四个区域抵达的战略安排有一个单一的目的。目标是为美联航在 EWR 的大量下午和晚间国际出发航班提供服务，以便所有潜在转机航班的载客率保持较高水平。网络调度员安排飞机在中午的转机班次降落，将地区乘客直接送入宽体客机出发，横跨大西洋飞往欧洲，再向南飞往拉丁美洲。
据 Deeparrival 报道，从夏洛茨维尔出发的 UA4414 航班将于下午 2:12 抵达纽瓦克，为旅客提供足够的缓冲，让他们顺利转乘跨大西洋的银行波，而无需忍受过多的航站楼停留。总体而言，这里使用的轴辐机制使支线航班不再像独立的点对点亏损领导者，而是成为支持高收益长途航线的更重要的收入来源。
这种精确的枢纽馈送使时间表延误的空间为零，主要是因为这些区域到达与下午宽体起飞紧密同步。因此，从夏洛茨维尔或诺克斯维尔出发的单一延迟入境轮换可能会导致高收益连接中断。纽瓦克的枢纽控制中心对这些到达流进行持续监督，当空中交通管制限制或局部拥堵威胁银行波的完整性时，部署战术缓解策略。

title_en: Nearly 2,000 Boeing 737s Must Get Tail Inspections After Jets Pitched Up And Down Mid-Flight
title_zh: 近 2,000 架波音 737 飞机在飞行途中上下颠簸后必须接受尾部检查
summary: The FAA warned of a potential loss of control as it ordered checks on nearly 2,000 Boeing 737NGs.
summary_zh: 美国联邦航空局 (FAA) 下令对近 2,000 架波音 737NG 进行检查，警告称可能会出现失控。
body_en: Nearly 2,000 Boeing 737s Must Get Tail Inspections After Jets Pitched Up And Down Mid-Flight

Luke has over a decade of experience as a travel writer and aviation analyst. As a passionate traveler based across the Middle East and Asia, Luke offers strong insights into the industry. Based in South East Asia.

The Federal Aviation Administration ( FAA ) has ordered inspections of nearly 2,000 Boeing 737 Next Generation (737NG) aircraft after multiple operators reported incidents in which the planes' noses moved up and down during flight. The airworthiness directive (AD) targets excessive movement in the hinges and jackscrew that support and move the aircraft's horizontal stabilizer.

The FAA warned that the issue could cause flutter and potentially lead to a loss of control if left unaddressed. The AD takes effect next month and covers a total of 1,987 US-registered Boeing 737NG aircraft, consisting of 737-600, -700, -700C, -800, -900 and -900ER models. The Boeing 737 MAX family is not affected by the directive.

AD 2026-20-14 takes effect on November 23 and requires airlines to measure excessive movement, also known as freeplay, at the left and right horizontal stabilizer pivot hinges and at the jackscrew. Depending on the results, operators may need to repeat the checks at specified intervals, or repair or replace worn parts.

The order follows several reports of pitch oscillation events due to excessive horizontal stabilizer freeplay on 737NG aircraft. The FAA did not specify how many pitch oscillation incidents were reported, when they occurred, or which airlines were involved.

On the 737, the horizontal stabilizer moves to adjust the aircraft's nose-up or nose-down position. It pivots on two hinges, while a jackscrew moves it into position. As these parts wear, freeplay can increase. If it becomes excessive, the stabilizer may experience flutter, potentially resulting in a loss of aircraft control. According to the FAA,
"The unsafe condition, if not addressed, could lead to a flutter event, which can result in loss of control of the airplane."
Airlines Requested More Time, The FAA Said No

The order was first proposed in January before being made final this week. At the time, several airlines and operators asked for more time or flexibility, including United Airlines , which has over 300 aircraft affected. United requested longer intervals between repeat inspections, as well as credit for checks already completed.

Meanwhile, Alaska Airlines asked to repair worn parts immediately rather than carry out interim freeplay checks. Canadian North also asked for the initial inspection deadline to be pushed back from 12 months to 36 months, allowing the work to coincide with heavy maintenance visits.

The FAA rejected these requests, saying the inspection intervals were to ensure excessive freeplay does not develop in either original or replacement parts. It is estimated that each inspection will take six work hours and cost $510 per aircraft, putting the cost across the US fleet at over $1 million, not including the price of replacement parts.

The FAA's directive currently covers US-registered 737NG models only, with authorities in other countries set to decide whether to mandate the same checks on aircraft registered in their jurisdictions. Data from ch-aviation shows there are over 5,160 737NG aircraft listed as active worldwide, while the 737-800 is the most common commercial jet model in service in the US today.

The world's largest Boeing 737 operator is Southwest Airlines , which has more than 800 737-family jets in service, over 500 of which are -700 and -800 models. Irish ultra-low-cost giant Ryanair is second with over 400 737NGs, followed by United and American Airlines .

Boeing delivered more than 7,000 737NGs between 1997 and January 2020, when the last jets were handed over. The fleet has faced widespread inspections before. In 2019, cracks in the "pickle fork" structure connecting the wings to the fuselage led the FAA to order inspections on US-registered 737NGs, also leading to dozens of aircraft being grounded worldwide.
body_zh: 近 2,000 架波音 737 飞机在飞行途中上下颠簸后必须接受尾部检查
卢克拥有十多年的旅行作家和航空分析师经验。作为一名遍及中东和亚洲的热情旅行者，卢克对该行业提供了深刻的见解。总部位于东南亚。
在多家运营商报告飞机机头在飞行过程中上下移动的事件后，美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 已下令对近 2,000 架下一代波音 737 (737NG) 飞机进行检查。适航指令（AD）针对的是支撑和移动飞机水平安定面的铰链和螺旋千斤顶的过度运动。
美国联邦航空局警告说，如果不解决这个问题可能会导致颤振并可能导致失控。该广告将于下个月生效，涵盖总共1,987架在美国注册的波音737NG飞机，包括737-600、-700、-700C、-800、-900和-900ER型号。波音 737 MAX 系列不受该指令的影响。
AD 2026-20-14 于 11 月 23 日生效，要求航空公司测量左右水平安定面枢轴铰链和螺旋千斤顶的过度运动（也称为自由运动）。根据结果​​，操作员可能需要按照指定的时间间隔重复检查，或者修理或更换磨损的部件。
该命令是在有关 737NG 飞机因水平安定面过度自由发挥而导致的俯仰振荡事件的多份报告之后发出的。美国联邦航空局没有具体说明报告了多少起俯仰振荡事件、发生时间以及涉及哪些航空公司。
在 737 上，水平安定面移动以调整飞机的机头向上或机头向下的位置。它通过两个铰链旋转，同时用螺旋千斤顶将其移动到位。随着这些部件的磨损，自由发挥会增加。如果过度，稳定器可能会颤动，可能导致飞机失控。据美国联邦航空局称，
“如果不解决这种不安全情况，可能会导致颤振事件，从而导致飞机失控。”
航空公司要求更多时间，美国联邦航空局拒绝
该命令于一月份首次提出，本周最终确定。当时，多家航空公司和运营商要求更多时间或灵活性，其中包括联合航空公司，该公司有 300 多架飞机受到影响。联合航空要求延长重复检查之间的间隔，并对已完成的检查给予信用。
与此同时，阿拉斯加航空公司要求立即修复磨损部件，而不是进行临时自由检查。加拿大北方公司还要求将最初检查的最后期限从 12 个月推迟到 36 个月，以便该工作能够与大量维护访问同时进行。
美国联邦航空局拒绝了这些请求，称检查间隔是为了确保原始零件或替换零件不会出现过度的自由间隙。据估计，每次检查将需要六个工作小时，每架飞机的成本为 510 美元，这使得整个美国机队的成本超过 100 万美元，这还不包括更换零件的价格。
FAA 的指令目前仅涵盖在美国注册的 737NG 型号，其他国家/地区的当局将决定是否对在其管辖范围内注册的飞机强制执行相同的检查。 ch-aviation 的数据显示，全球有超过 5,160 架 737NG 飞机处于活跃状态，而 737-800 是当今美国现役最常见的商用喷气机型号。
全球最大的波音 737 运营商是西南航空，该公司拥有 800 多架在役 737 系列飞机，其中 500 多架为 -700 和 -800 型号。爱尔兰超低成本巨头瑞安航空 (Ryanair) 拥有 400 多架 737NG 飞机，位居第二，其次是联合航空 (United Airlines) 和美国航空 (American Airlines)。
1997 年至 2020 年 1 月期间交付了最后一批喷气式飞机，波音公司交付了超过 7,000 架 737NG。该船队此前曾接受过广泛的检查。 2019年，连接机翼和机身的“泡菜叉”结构出现裂缝，导致美国联邦航空局下令对美国注册的737NG进行检查，也导致全球数十架飞机停飞。

title_en: Here's Why Airlines Now Can't Live Without The Aircraft That Was Developed By A Regional Jet Maker
title_zh: 这就是为什么航空公司现在不能没有支线喷气式飞机制造商开发的飞机
summary: How the Airbus catapult Bombardier's small single-aisle to global success.
summary_zh: 空中客车公司如何使庞巴迪的小型单通道飞机在全球取得成功。
body_en: Here's Why Airlines Now Can't Live Without The Aircraft That Was Developed By A Regional Jet Maker

Luke Diaz is a freelance military writer with experience with active duty experience in the US Navy as well as defense and industrial engineering. He is a former Naval Flight Officer who performed tactical air control on the carrier-based E-2 Hawkeye.

Originally developed as the Bombardier CSeries, Airbus' increasingly popular small single-aisle jet was only able to achieve the success it is seeing today after it was rescued and rebranded by the European aerospace juggernaut as the A220. Despite an origin story that started in the clutches of abandonment, the A220 has since collected 1,107 orders and delivered 550 aircraft as of September, according to MRO Business Today.

The Montreal planemaker that first developed the plane that became the A220 had never built anything larger than a regional jet and envisioned the CSeries as its 'moonshot' to break up the Airbus-Boeing duopoly. Ultimately, making the 100 to 150-seat narrowbody proved to be too great a challenge, as development delays and cost overruns nearly bankrupted Bombardier. Airbus acquired a 50.01% controlling stake in the program for just $1 in 2018.

Bombardier fully withdrew after transferring its remaining 25% stake to Airbus in 2020. Today, Airbus owns 75% of the program, and the government of Quebec owns 25%. In the past six years, airlines worldwide have made the A220 a core pillar of their short-to-medium-haul networks because it occupies a highly profitable niche. Although the plane's creator did not achieve its dream of competing with the titans of commercial aviation, it remains a historic Underdog success story.
The Rising Success Of The A220 In A Narrow Market

Airbus delivered its 500th A220 in late March. The global fleet now flies with 25 operators on more than 1,900 routes. Airbus has also reported operational reliability of roughly 99%, numbers akin to a mature airliner rather than a risky new design. As one of the leading operators, Delta Air Lines shows what an A220 fleet looks like at scale. The small narrowbody has become a key tool for connecting hubs, not just a niche airframe for thin routes.

Cesium schedule data shows DAL scheduled 97,438 flights for its A220s in 2026, which produces an average of 267 every day. Few airlines would commit that much traffic to an aircraft they consider a dubious product. Likewise, JetBlue, Air France, airBaltic, and smaller regional lines like Breeze Airways have heavily invested in A220 orders to bolster their flightlines.

In May, AirAsia signed the program's largest single firm order, 150 A220-300s, according to the Canadian Press. All of those aircraft will be built at the Mirabel plant north of Montreal despite Bombardier's departure from the factory floor. What began as a multi-billion-dollar corporate gamble for an ambitious Canadian maker has matured into one of the single most industrially disruptive airliners in modern history.

The transformation of the Bombardier CSeries into the Airbus A220 stands as one of the most unusual chapters in modern aviation. While the infrastructure, sales, and supply chain of Airbus ultimately saved the aircraft from ruin, the airplane flying today is mechanically the exact machine designed by Bombardier. Airbus made virtually no changes to the clean-sheet design after taking the helm.

Airbus describes the A220 as the only aircraft purpose-built for the small end of the single-aisle market. The advanced aerodynamics, heavy use of weight-saving lithium-aluminum alloys, and carbon-fiber composite wings were all developed during Bombardier’s tenure. The integration of the Pratt & Whitney Geared Turbofan engine was already decided. The aircraft was already certified and carrying passengers when program ownership was abdicated by Montreal's famed planemaker.

The program's irony is that Bombardier achieved total engineering success but suffered total industrial failure. By absorbing the program into its global network, Airbus brought immediate credibility to the order book. It also applied its immense supply chain leverage to drive down production costs. To bypass crippling American tariffs that threatened the program, Airbus even established a second assembly line in Mobile, Alabama, a move only its industrial might could replicate.
The Winning Combo Of Low Operating Costs And Cabin Comfort

Cost is where the case becomes convincing. Airbus claims the A220 burns 25% less fuel per seat than the previous generation of small single-aisle jets, with a similar cut in emissions. However, in the cabin, passenger comfort is the first thing travelers notice. The CSeries, and the A220 that followed, was designed as a regional jet that delivers a single-aisle cabin experience.

The company also says it offers up to 20 more seats than some competitors and up to 14% lower operating cost per seat. Business class cabins on an A220 offer four seats across at 21 inches (53.3 cm) wide, and extra-large overhead bins add 20% more volume.

Meanwhile, economy seats measure more than 18 inches (47 centimeters) wide, and the middle seat in each row of five stretches to 19 inches (48.3 centimeters). Two seats sit on one side of the aisle and three on the other. The windows measure 11 by 16 inches (28 by 41 centimeters), and the ceiling is four inches (10.1 centimeters) higher than on competing jets.

The A220 has proven especially well suited to replace the venerable Embraer E190, a popular regional plane in the US domestic market for decades. JetBlue, for example, was the launch customer of the Brazilian-built workhorse, but it has already received over 50 A220s to modernize the smaller end of its fleet, and that's just half of its total order. Not only does the A220 offer superior fuel efficiency and more legroom, but it also provides greater seat capacity and longer range, which means it is an upgauge and an upgrade over the legacy E-jets it often replaces.

Operating a specialized 140-seat configuration on its A220-300 variants, JetBlue purposefully keeps the passenger count below the aircraft's maximum exit limit to augment the plane's transcontinental range. That allows for flights from JetBlue's primary hub at New York JFK to secondary western fields like Reno-Tahoe and Hollywood Burbank in California. The carrier has also been able to deploy A220s on long-range coast-to-coast flights from Boston Logan to West Coast destinations like Sacramento, California, and Portland, Oregon.
Delta Maximizes Network Flexibility With Airbus' Light Single-Aisle

Delta has pushed the A220 to its maximum potential, using it as the backbone for Midwestern and West Coast inter-hub 'puddle jumps' as well as a connector between large fields and regional airports. Salt Lake City International Airport (SLC) has become the world's largest hub for A220 operations, as DAL designed the airfield as the jet's primary launchpad while overhauling its entire regional operation.
body_zh: 这就是为什么航空公司现在不能没有支线喷气式飞机制造商开发的飞机
卢克·迪亚兹 (Luke Diaz) 是一位自由军事作家，拥有在美国海军以及国防和工业工程领域服役的现役经验。他是一名前海军飞行军官，曾在舰载 E-2 鹰眼上执行战术空中控制。
空客这款日益流行的小型单通道喷气式飞机最初开发为庞巴迪 C 系列，直到被欧洲航空航天巨头拯救并重新命名为 A220 后才取得今天的成功。据《MRO Business Today》报道，尽管 A220 的起源故事始于废弃，但截至 9 月份，A220 已收到 1,107 份订单并交付了 550 架飞机。
首先开发 A220 飞机的蒙特利尔飞机制造商从未制造过比支线喷气式飞机更大的飞机，并将 CSeries 视为打破空客-波音双头垄断的“登月计划”。最终，事实证明，制造 100 至 150 座的窄体飞机是一项巨大的挑战，因为开发延迟和成本超支几乎让庞巴迪破产。 2018年，空中客车公司仅以1美元的价格收购了该项目50.01%的控股权。
庞巴迪在2020年将剩余的25%股权转让给空客后全面退出。如今，空客拥有该项目75%的股份，魁北克政府拥有25%的股份。在过去的六年里，世界各地的航空公司都将A220作为其中短程网络的核心支柱，因为它占据了高利润的利基市场。尽管这架飞机的创造者未能实现与商业航空巨头竞争的梦想，但它仍然是一个历史性的失败者成功故事。
A220 在狭窄的市场中不断取得成功
空中客车公司于 3 月底交付了第 500 架 A220。全球机队目前由 25 家运营商运营，运营超过 1,900 条航线。空中客车公司还报告称，运营可靠性约为 99%，这一数字类似于成熟的客机，而不是有风险的新设计。作为领先的运营商之一，达美航空展示了 A220 机队的规模。小型窄体飞机已成为连接枢纽的关键工具，而不仅仅是用于细航线的利基机身。
Cesium时刻表数据显示，DAL在2026年为其A220飞机安排了97,438个航班，平均每天产生267个航班。很少有航空公司会向他们认为可疑产品的飞机投入如此多的流量。同样，捷蓝航空、法国航空、波罗的海航空和微风航空等较小的支线航空公司也大力投资 A220 订单，以加强其航线。
据加拿大媒体报道，5 月，亚航签署了该计划最大的单一确定订单，即 150 架 A220-300 飞机。尽管庞巴迪已离开工厂，但所有这些飞机都将在蒙特利尔北部的米拉贝尔工厂建造。最初是一家雄心勃勃的加拿大制造商进行的数十亿美元的企业赌博，现已发展成为现代历史上最具工业颠覆性的客机之一。
庞巴迪 CSeries 向空客 A220 的转变是现代航空业最不寻常的篇章之一。虽然空客的基础设施、销售和供应链最终使飞机免遭毁灭，但今天飞行的飞机在机械上与庞巴迪设计的机器完全相同。空中客车公司掌舵后几乎没有对干净的设计进行任何改变。
空中客车公司将 A220 描述为唯一一款专为单通道小端市场打造的飞机。先进的空气动力学、大量使用减重锂铝合金以及碳纤维复合材料机翼都是庞巴迪在任期间开发的。普惠齿轮涡轮风扇发动机的集成已经决定。当蒙特利尔著名的飞机制造商放弃项目所有权时，这架飞机已经获得认证并可以载客。
该计划的讽刺之处在于，庞巴迪在工程上取得了全面的成功，但在工业上却遭遇了全面的失败。通过将该项目纳入其全球网络，空客立即为订单带来了可信度。它还利用其巨大的供应链杠杆来降低生产成本。为了绕过威胁该计划的美国关税，空客甚至在阿拉巴马州莫比尔建立了第二条装配线，这一举措只有其工业部门才能复制。
低运营成本和客舱舒适度的制胜组合
成本是案例变得有说服力的地方。空中客车公司声称，与上一代小型单通道喷气式飞机相比，A220 每个座位的燃油消耗减少了 25%，排放量也有类似的减少。然而，在机舱内，乘客的舒适度是旅客首先注意到的。 CSeries 和随后的 A220 被设计为支线喷气式飞机，提供单通道客舱体验。
该公司还表示，它比一些竞争对手多提供了 20 个座位，每个座位的运营成本降低了 14%。 A220 的商务舱设有四个宽度为 21 英寸（53.3 厘米）的座椅，超大头顶行李箱增加了 20% 的容积。
与此同时，经济舱座位的宽度超过 18 英寸（47 厘米），每排 5 个座位​​的中间座位宽度达到 19 英寸（48.3 厘米）。两个座位位于过道的一侧，三个座位位于过道的另一侧。窗户尺寸为 11 x 16 英寸（28 x 41 厘米），天花板比竞争对手的喷气式飞机高 4 英寸（10.1 厘米）。

事实证明，A220 特别适合取代久负盛名的巴西航空工业公司 E190，后者是几十年来在美国国内市场上广受欢迎的支线飞机。例如，捷蓝航空是这架巴西制造的主力飞机的首发客户，但它已经收到了 50 多架 A220 飞机，用于对其机队规模较小的部分进行现代化改造，而这只是其总订单的一半。 A220 不仅提供卓越的燃油效率和更大的腿部空间，而且还提供更大的座位容量和更远的航程，这意味着它是对其经常取代的传统电动喷气式飞机的升级和升级。
捷蓝航空在其 A220-300 机型上采用专门的 140 座配置，有目的地将乘客数量保持在飞机的最大出口限制以下，以扩大飞机的横贯大陆范围。这使得捷蓝航空可以从纽约肯尼迪机场的主要枢纽飞往加州的里诺太浩湖和好莱坞伯班克等西部次要枢纽。该航空公司还能够在从波士顿洛根飞往加利福尼亚州萨克拉门托和俄勒冈州波特兰等西海岸目的地的远程海岸到海岸航班上部署 A220。
达美航空利用空客轻型单通道飞机最大限度地提高网络灵活性
达美航空充分发挥了 A220 的最大潜力，将其用作中西部和西海岸枢纽间“水坑跳跃”的骨干，以及大型油田和支线机场之间的连接器。盐湖城国际机场 (SLC) 已成为全球最大的 A220 运营中心，DAL 将机场设计为飞机的主要发射台，同时对其整个区域运营进行了彻底改革。

title_en: What Are The Benefits Of Flying On Emirates’ Airbus A380?
title_zh: 乘坐阿联酋航空空客 A380 有什么好处？
summary: The Emirates A380 experience can provide unparalleled comfort and luxury.
summary_zh: 阿联酋航空 A380 体验可提供无与伦比的舒适和奢华。
body_en: What Are The Benefits Of Flying On Emirates’ Airbus A380?

A graduate in German, Jake has a passion for history and regional aviation, and enjoys sampling new carriers and aircraft. He has visited OEM facilities as far and wide as Bristol, Toulouse, and Seattle, and recently enjoyed the milestone of flying his 150th sector as a passenger. Based in Norfolk, UK.

For many travelers, the Airbus A380 has become more than just another aircraft type. Even as airlines around the world have retired the superjumbo, Emirates has continued to operate the world’s largest A380 fleet and position it as a defining part of its long-haul product. This has led to a common question among passengers and aviation enthusiasts alike: what are the real benefits of flying on Emirates’ Airbus A380?

In this article, we will explore why the Emirates A380 experience feels distinct, looking beyond headline features to examine how aircraft design, cabin layout, and operational strategy shape the overall journey. We will do so by breaking down the physical characteristics of the A380, Emirates’ approach to configuring and deploying it, and how the experience compares with alternatives such as the Boeing 777 .

The key benefit of flying on Emirates’ Airbus A380 is that it delivers a noticeably calmer, more comfortable long-haul experience than most other widebody aircraft. This is not simply because the A380 is larger, but because its design creates more usable space per passenger, reducing noise, congestion, and the feeling of crowding .

Even before considering premium features, the aircraft feels fundamentally different once onboard when compared with other airline products or aircraft types. Emirates has amplified these advantages more than any other airline by treating the A380 as more of a flagship rather than a mere capacity tool.

The airline’s cabin layouts, upper-deck design, and onboard amenities are built around passenger comfort, regardless of whether that be in economy, business, or first class. As a result, travelers often describe the A380 as quieter, smoother, and less fatiguing on long sectors compared to aircraft like the Boeing 777, even when flying in the same cabin class.

This experience is rooted in how the A380 was originally conceived. Airbus designed the aircraft around cabin volume and stability at a time when congestion and passenger comfort were growing concerns, while Emirates structured its network to take full advantage of those characteristics. The combination helps explain why the A380 remains a standout experience at Emirates today, even as many other airlines have moved away from the type.

Several design and operational factors combine to shape why flying on Emirates’ A380 feels different from other long-haul aircraft. While size plays a role, the experience is more heavily influenced by how that space is used, how the aircraft behaves in flight, and how Emirates has configured its cabins around passenger flow rather than maximum density.

Together, these elements affect everything from boarding to how the aircraft feels hours into a long journey. One of the most important factors is cabin volume. The A380’s wide fuselage allows for broader aisles, larger galleys, and more open seating areas, which helps reduce congestion during boarding, meal services, and, very importantly, lavatory queues.

The aircraft is also inherently quieter and more stable in cruise, thanks to its size and four-engine configuration , which dampens vibration and turbulence. Emirates further enhances these characteristics through consistent seat layouts and upper-deck zoning that separate premium cabins from the main-deck economy flow.

The carrier has effectively mastered the A380 experience through consistent refinement of the aircraft's internal space. These factors are especially noticeable on long-haul sectors, where small comfort differences compound over time. Passengers frequently report that boarding feels less chaotic, cabin movement is easier during the flight, and the overall atmosphere is calmer compared to similarly long flights on narrower widebodies.

While Emirates’ service and amenities play a prominent role in making A380 services so different from competitors, much of this experience is rooted in the A380’s physical design, which gives the airline more flexibility to prioritize comfort without sacrificing capacity.

Emirates has consistently positioned the Airbus A380 as the centerpiece of its overall long-haul product, rather than simply one aircraft type among many. On its official fleet pages , the airline highlights the A380’s role in delivering space, comfort, and onboard features that would be difficult to replicate on smaller widebodies, by comparison.

This strategy reflects a broader airline philosophy that prioritizes the onboard experience as a key differentiator, particularly on ultra-long-haul routes where comfort becomes a decisive factor for passengers. That positioning is reinforced by how the aircraft is configured and presented to passengers.

Emirates’ published A380 seating charts show a deliberate emphasis on upper-deck separation, generous premium cabin layouts, and dedicated social spaces, rather than maximizing overall seat seat density. Passenger feedback broadly aligns with this approach. Online discussions and travel-related forums frequently point to the A380’s calm cabin environment, particularly on the upper deck, as a defining feature of the experience.

Rather than focusing exclusively on headline amenities, many travelers emphasize how the aircraft feels less congested during boarding and more relaxed in flight, suggesting that Emirates’ A380 reputation is built as much on atmosphere and spatial design as it is on luxury branding.

When compared with other widebody aircraft, the Emirates A380 stands out less for any single feature and more for how its overall design changes the passenger experience. Aircraft like the Boeing 777 or Airbus A350 are highly efficient and technologically advanced, but they operate within tighter cabin volumes that naturally limit how space can be distributed onboard .

As a result, even well-designed cabins can feel busier, particularly during boarding and peak service periods. The A380’s double-deck layout fundamentally alters that dynamic. By separating cabins vertically rather than compressing them longitudinally, Emirates is able to reduce foot traffic through premium areas, limit cross-cabin congestion, and create quieter zones, especially on the upper deck, where this unique characteristic is of particular note.

These factors are most noticeable in business and first class, where passengers rarely experience through-traffic from other cabins. By contrast, Emirates’ Boeing 777 fleet, while offering modern seats and a strong onboard product, cannot replicate the same sense of openness or calm simply due to physical constraints.
body_zh: 乘坐阿联酋航空空客 A380 有什么好处？

杰克毕业于德语，对历史和支线航空充满热情，并喜欢尝试新的航母和飞机。他参观过远至布里斯托尔、图卢兹和西雅图的 OEM 工厂，最近还享受了作为乘客飞行第 150 个航段的里程碑。总部位于英国诺福克。
对于许多旅客来说，空客 A380 已不仅仅是另一种飞机类型。尽管世界各地的航空公司已经退役了超级客机，但阿联酋航空仍继续运营着全球最大的 A380 机队，并将其定位为其长途产品的重要组成部分。这引发了乘客和航空爱好者的一个共同问题：乘坐阿联酋航空空客 A380 的真正好处是什么？

在本文中，我们将探讨为什么阿联酋航空 A380 的体验感觉与众不同，超越标题特征，研究飞机设计、机舱布局和运营策略如何塑造整体旅程。为此，我们将详细介绍 A380 的物理特性、阿联酋航空配置和部署 A380 的方法，以及其体验与波音 777 等替代机型的比较。
乘坐阿联酋航空空客 A380 的主要优势在于，与大多数其他宽体飞机相比，它可以提供明显更平静、更舒适的长途体验。这不仅仅是因为 A380 更大，还因为它的设计为每位乘客创造了更多的可用空间，减少了噪音、拥堵和拥挤感。
即使在考虑高级功能之前，与其他航空公司产品或飞机类型相比，飞机登机后的感觉也有根本不同。阿联酋航空将 A380 视为旗舰而不是单纯的运力工具，从而比任何其他航空公司都更加放大了这些优势。
该航空公司的客舱布局、上层甲板设计和机上设施均以乘客舒适度为中心，无论是经济舱、商务舱还是头等舱。因此，与波音 777 等飞机相比，旅客经常将 A380 形容为更安静、更平稳，并且在长途飞行中更不易疲劳，即使是在同一舱位飞行时也是如此。
这种体验植根于 A380 的最初构想。在拥堵和乘客舒适度日益受到关注的时代，空中客车公司围绕机舱容积和稳定性设计了飞机，而阿联酋航空则构建了其网络以充分利用这些特征。这一组合有助于解释为什么 A380 至今仍然是阿联酋航空的出色体验，尽管许多其他航空公司已经放弃了该机型。
多个设计和操作因素共同决定了为什么乘坐阿联酋航空 A380 的飞行感觉与其他长途飞机有所不同。虽然尺寸发挥着重要作用，但体验在很大程度上取决于空间的使用方式、飞机在飞行中的表现以及阿联酋航空如何围绕客流而不是最大密度配置机舱。
这些因素共同影响着一切，从登机到长途旅行几个小时后的飞机感受。最重要的因素之一是机舱容积。 A380 的宽机身允许更宽的过道、更大的厨房和更开放的座位区，这有助于减少登机、餐饮服务以及非常重要的厕所排队期间的拥堵。
由于其尺寸和四引擎配置，该飞机在巡航时也更安静、更稳定，可以抑制振动和湍流。阿联酋航空通过一致的座椅布局和上层甲板分区，将高级客舱与主甲板经济舱分开，进一步增强了这些特征。
通过对飞机内部空间的不断完善，该航空公司有效地掌握了A380的经验。这些因素在长途航线上尤其明显，随着时间的推移，微小的舒适度差异会加剧。乘客经常反映，与窄体宽体客机的类似长途飞行相比，登机感觉不那么混乱，飞行过程中机舱移动更容易，整体氛围更平静。

title_en: FAA orders checks on nearly 2,000 Boeing 737s after pitch oscillation events
title_zh: 俯仰振荡事件发生后，FAA 下令对近 2,000 架波音 737 进行检查
summary: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has ordered inspections of nearly 2,000 Boeing 737 Next Generation aircraft after… The post FAA orders checks on nearly 2,000 Boeing 737s after pitch oscillation events appeared first on AeroTime .
summary_zh: 美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 已下令对近 2,000 架下一代波音 737 飞机进行检查……
body_en: The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has ordered inspections of nearly 2,000 Boeing 737 Next Generation aircraft after multiple operators reported pitch oscillations linked to excessive looseness in the horizontal stabilizer mechanism.

The airworthiness directive, published on October 19, 2026, requires operators to measure movement in the stabilizer’s pivot hinges and jackscrew, then carry out additional checks, repairs or parts replacements depending on the findings.
The FAA estimates that 1,987 US-registered aircraft are affected. The directive covers 737-600, -700, -700C, -800, -900 and -900ER aircraft. It does not apply to the 737 MAX.
The rule takes effect on November 23, 2026, with inspections due according to the compliance schedule incorporated into the directive.

The horizontal stabilizer is the movable horizontal surface on the aircraft’s tail that helps control its nose-up or nose-down attitude. Excessive movement within its supporting mechanism, known as freeplay, can allow unwanted motion.

The FAA said the reported pitch oscillations were caused by excessive stabilizer freeplay and warned that leaving the condition uncorrected could lead to flutter, a potentially dangerous vibration that can result in loss of control.
The final directive follows a proposed rule published in January 2026 and incorporates inspection procedures detailed in a Boeing bulletin from June 12, 2025.

Some airlines sought adjustments to the inspection requirements during the public comment period. Canadian North asked the FAA to extend the initial inspection threshold from 12 months to 36 months, arguing that the longer period would allow the work to coincide with heavy maintenance visits and give operators more time to arrange parts and labor.
United Airlines requested longer repeat inspection intervals for aircraft fitted with replacement hinge bearings, compared with those retaining their original parts.

The FAA rejected both requests. It said the inspection schedule was necessary to maintain an acceptable level of safety and that excessive freeplay needed to be monitored whether components were original, repaired or newly installed.
The agency said it would consider individual requests for extensions if operators supplied sufficient evidence that an alternative schedule would maintain safety.

The agency estimates that the freeplay measurement will require six work-hours per aircraft, costing $510 at its assumed labor rate of $85 an hour. Across the affected US fleet, that amounts to approximately $1 million.

Additional inspections and repairs would increase those costs. The FAA said it could not determine how many aircraft would need replacement components and did not have definitive prices for the worn parts that might require replacement.
