body_zh: 在多家运营商报告水平安定面机构过度松动导致俯仰振荡后，美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 已下令对近 2,000 架下一代波音 737 飞机进行检查。
2026 年 10 月 19 日发布的适航指令要求运营商测量稳定器枢轴铰链和螺旋千斤顶的运动，然后根据结果进行额外的检查、维修或零件更换。
FAA 估计有 1,987 架在美国注册的飞机受到影响。该指令涵盖 737-600、-700、-700C、-800、-900 和 -900ER 飞机。它不适用于 737 MAX。
该规则于 2026 年 11 月 23 日生效，并根据指令中纳入的合规时间表进行检查。
水平稳定器是飞机尾部的可移动水平表面，有助于控制机头向上或机头向下的姿态。其支撑机构内的过度运动（称为自由运动）可能会导致不必要的运动。
美国联邦航空局表示，报告的俯仰振荡是由稳定器过度自由运动引起的，并警告说，如果不纠正这种情况可能会导致颤振，这是一种潜在的危险振动，可能导致失控。
最终指令遵循 2026 年 1 月发布的拟议规则，并纳入了 2025 年 6 月 12 日波音公告中详细介绍的检查程序。
一些航空公司在公众意见征询期间寻求调整检查要求。加拿大北方公司要求美国联邦航空局将初始检查期限从 12 个月延长至 36 个月，理由是更长的期限可以让工作与繁重的维护访问同时进行，并让运营商有更多的时间来安排零件和劳动力。
与保留原始部件的飞机相比，美国联合航空公司要求对装有替换铰链轴承的飞机进行更长的重复检查间隔。
美国联邦航空局拒绝了这两项请求。它表示，检查计划对于保持可接受的安全水平是必要的，并且需要监控过度的自由发挥，无论组件是原装的、修理过的还是新安装的。
该机构表示，如果运营商提供足够的证据证明替代时间表可以保证安全，它将考虑个人的延期请求。
该机构估计，自由活动测量将需要每架飞机 6 个小时的工作时间，按照每小时 85 美元的假设劳动费率计算，成本为 510 美元。受影响的美国机队损失金额约为 100 万美元。
额外的检查和维修会增加这些成本。美国联邦航空局表示，无法确定有多少架飞机需要更换部件，也没有可能需要更换的磨损部件的明确价格。
在 AeroTime 首次出现俯仰振荡事件后，美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 下令对近 2,000 架波音 737 进行检查。

title_zh: 捷蓝航空股价跌至历史最低点，债权人请来重组专家
summary: The carrier's turnaround faces mounting pressure as fuel costs soar and creditors grow concerned.
summary_zh: 随着燃油成本飙升和债权人日益担忧，该航空公司的扭亏为盈面临着越来越大的压力。
body_en: JetBlue Creditors Call In Restructuring Experts As Shares Plummet To All-Time Low

A group of JetBlue's major creditors has hired restructuring advisers after the airline's shares hit record lows, raising questions about how the carrier will manage its debt while trying to return to profitability. According to The Wall Street Journal , the creditors have brought in financial adviser PJT Partners and law firm Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld, citing people familiar with the matter.

The move follows a difficult year for JetBlue , which reportedly explored a potential sale to rivals, including United Airlines . The appointment of restructuring advisers does not mean bankruptcy or major operational changes are imminent, but it adds to growing concerns about the carrier's struggling financial position.
JetBlue Faces Mounting Pressure To Turn Its Business Around

The creditor group includes holders of JetBlue's $2 billion in bonds due in 2031 and a $742 million first-lien loan. The New York-based carrier's stock dropped nearly 10% on Thursday to close at $2.65, its lowest level since it went public in 2002. In fact, its shares have plummeted by 42% so far this year amid a sharp rise in jet fuel prices.

JetBlue has spent the past two years trying to improve its performance through JetForward, a plan launched in July 2024 under CEO Joanna Geraghty. This focuses on controlling costs and making better use of the airline's network and aircraft. While the airline has made progress, higher operating costs have made a sustained recovery more difficult.

JetBlue recorded a $247 million net loss in the second quarter, even as revenue increased 14.5% year-on-year to $2.7 billion. In a statement to Reuters , JetBlue said it " remains confident in its JetForward strategy " and pointed to progress toward achieving sustained profitability.

Reports also emerged earlier this year that JetBlue had explored a possible sale to another airline , with United, Alaska Airlines and Southwest Airlines named as potential buyers. United CEO Scott Kirby was asked about JetBlue during a recent earnings call, but said he had " nothing new to add on that ."

Rising fuel prices have become a significant problem for airlines globally. US jet fuel prices have nearly doubled since late February, with JetBlue's average fuel price skyrocketing by 76% to $4.23 per gallon in the second quarter. Additionally, the airline raised its estimate for third-quarter fuel costs in September.

Like most major US airlines, JetBlue does not hedge a significant amount of its fuel, leaving it exposed to sudden price increases. As of June 30, the airline had $8.5 billion in debt and finance lease obligations, while S&P Global Ratings recently downgraded the airline, citing pressure from higher fuel prices.

JetBlue's third-quarter results on October 27 could offer clues about whether its turnaround is progressing quickly enough to reassure lenders and investors. Meanwhile, for passengers, there is no indication that JetBlue's current flight schedule or onboard offerings will change.

Despite the financial pressure, JetBlue continues to invest in its product and network as it looks to attract more passengers and increase revenue per flight. One of its most significant moves is the introduction of BlueFirst, a new domestic first-class cabin on flights that do not feature its Mint business-class product.

Earlier this month, the carrier opened bookings for BlueFirst on more than 30 routes, with the first service scheduled between Boston Logan (BOS) and Fort Lauderdale (FLL) on December 8. Among the perks of the new cabin are wider recliner seats, complimentary meals, premium snacks and drinks, and priority services.

The carrier is also strengthening its network at key airports. This includes Fort Lauderdale — where it increased capacity by nearly 40% after Spirit Airlines folded — and at its bases in New York and Boston. Air France and KLM have been issued fines by the US Department Of Transportation after it was revealed that both European carriers operated Delta Air Lines codeshare flights below 32,000 feet above Iraq. The fines were issued due to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) prohibiting flights by US operators in foreign-managed airspace where conflict or heightened tensions threaten safety.

Foreign airlines with US airline codes, such as the Delta codeshare, must also abide by these prohibitions. Air France has been given a $105,000 fine, while KLM will be expected to pay a sum of $320,000 after both carriers were found to have violated FAA restrictions while operating flights with Delta designator codes .

Air France & KLM Charged For Operating More Than 100 Flights In Prohibited Airspace

The Office of Aviation Consumer Protection (OACP) conducted a thorough investigation of both airlines' operations, revealing that Air France operated more than 30 flights with a Delta codeshare, while KLM flew more than 100 flights with the Delta code in FAA-prohibited airspace in the Baghdad Flight Information Region between January 2022 and May 2025.

While Delta itself did not operate the flights, their flight numbers were placed on the Air France and KLM services through a marketing arrangement where the airline placed its designator code on the SkyTeam alliance partners and sold tickets for these flights on the two airlines. US Transportation Secretary Sean P. Duffy said :

“Under the Trump Administration, if you fly carrying a US code, following our safety rules is not optional. We will not hesitate to hold accountable any airline for failing to comply with agency regulations. Passenger safety comes first—no exceptions.”
A Combined $425,000 in Penalties Issued By The DOT

The action taken by the DOT is based on the instance where both airlines were reported to have flown below 32,000 feet in the Baghdad region. The allegations, which have dated back to the beginning of 2022, have seen both Air France and KLM dispute responsibility for altitude deviations, suggesting that air traffic controllers were directing the aircraft's altitude.

A central question that has been raised is whether the airlines should be penalized for operating below the prohibited altitude when following instructions from ATC. Both airlines ultimately now face a combined penalty of $425,000, with $265,000 due within the next 60 days, and the remaining $160,000 only payable if either airline commits a similar violation within the next year.

Both airlines have explained to the US DOT that they take regulatory compliance seriously, and neither airline deliberately ignored the restrictions. The uniqueness of this situation is that while neither airline is a US carrier, the US government expects safety-related restrictions to be followed by foreign operators if marked with a US airline designator. title_en: Overachiever: The Only F-117 To Fly Combat In 4 Conflicts Finally Reaches The Smithsonian
title_zh: 卓越者：唯一一架在 4 场冲突中进行飞行战斗的 F-117 最终到达史密森学会

body_en: Overachiever: The Only F-117 To Fly Combat In 4 Conflicts Finally Reaches The Smithsonian

Luke Diaz is a freelance military writer with experience with active duty experience in the US Navy as well as defense and industrial engineering. He is a former Naval Flight Officer who performed tactical air control on the carrier-based E-2 Hawkeye.

The Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum announced on September 14 that it would finally receive its first example of the legendary Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk. This particular airframe is affectionately known as 'overachiever' for its enduring service that spanned four conflicts, from the very first missions ever flown by a stealth plane into combat to the major air campaign of Operation Iraqi Freedom. As of October 6, the jet was inducted for its final display preparations at a special hangar on the field of Washington Dulles International Airport (IAD) in DC.

Notably, despite the retirement of the Nighthawk from Frontline service, a select few remain in the official inventory. The US Air Force officially sunset the F-117 in 2008, just a few years after tail number 85-0818 flew its final combat sortie. Yet, it still flies a small cadre of Nighthawks at remote airfields in the American Southwest and has even indicated plans to keep doing so until at least 2034.

The arrival of the iconic angular black jet is a milestone addition to the already unparalleled collection at the expansive museum in the Steven F. Udvar-Hazy Center of Chantilly, Virginia. As the first operational aircraft built with true stealth technology, the F-117 kicked off the race for low-observable, radar-defeating technology that defines the modern era of air warfare. Overachiever is a very carefully curated airframe with its decorated history of service, making it a must-see attraction for Av Geeks visiting the nation's capital.

The F-117A made its combat debut on December 19, 1989, with Operation Just Cause. Six aircraft from the 37th Tactical Fighter Wing launched from Tonopah, Nevada, on a long-range mission that would require five aerial refuelings. The primary mission was an infrastructure strike at Rio Hato airfield, home to Panama Defense Forces Battalion 2000. Planners aimed to stun the sleeping garrison to clear the way for a low-level drop by US Army Rangers flying in on transports on the heels of the strike.

The tactical plan required precise timing to detonate conventional bombs 30 seconds before the paratroopers arrived. At 1:01 AM, Captain Gregory Feest dropped a 2,000-lb (907 kg) GBU-27 laser-guided bomb next to the barracks, causing a shockwave that shattered windows and sent the local forces into chaotic disarray.

A last-minute change in targeting, wind shifts, and technical errors caused the second F-117A's bomb to drift off target. The surprise attack was also compromised by a leak that had allowed some PDF troops to evacuate the buildings before impact.

Despite failing to achieve all the original objectives, the Joint Chiefs of Staff deemed the mission an operational success. The psychological shock of the stealth attack delayed the PDF counterattack, allowing the Rangers to secure a vital runway after a five-hour firefight. The F-117As exited Panamanian airspace with impunity, validating the stealth concept for the first time in a real-world combat environment.

The Nighthawk's second foray into battle proved to be a defining chapter in the warbird's legacy. As Operation Desert Storm commenced, F-117s took off in the early hours of January 17, 1991. The conflict would solidify the importance of low-observable combat planes, proving that a subsonic aircraft could infiltrate the most densely defended airspace on Earth completely unassisted thanks to stealth. Prior to the war, planners viewed an air assault on Baghdad as potentially suicidal due to sophisticated Soviet integrated air defenses linked to a central command system code-named 'Kari.'

Against Kari, conventional aircraft required massive escort packages of radar jammers, fighter escorts, and anti-radiation platforms just to survive. The F-117 upended this dynamic entirely. Operating from remote bases in Saudi Arabia, the 37th TFW deployed their aircraft to fly as lone, independent platforms. They bypassed radar screens without electronic jamming escorts that would otherwise tip off Iraqi controllers.

At 2:51 AM on night one, the first laser-guided bomb dropped by a Nighthawk struck a telecommunications tower in downtown Baghdad, instantly severing Iraqi command-and-control. Follow-on aircraft struck air defense headquarters, sector operation bunkers, and presidential palaces. Because Iraqi operators could not track the stealth aircraft, they resorted to blind saturation fire, filling the night sky with thousands of anti-aircraft rounds. Despite flying through heavy flak, 29 F-117s successfully hit over two dozen high-value targets.

The final battle metrics underscored the asymmetric advantage of stealth technology. While the F-117 fleet comprised a mere 2.5% of total coalition aircraft, the jets struck roughly 40% of all high-value strategic targets during the first three days of the war. Over the six-week campaign, the fleet logged 1,271 combat sorties and more than 6,900 flight hours. Despite flying into the teeth of anti-aircraft fire night after night, not a single Nighthawk was damaged or lost to hostile fire.

The illusion of absolute stealth invulnerability was shattered on March 27, 1999, on a mission under NATO’s Operation Allied Force over Yugoslavia. The paradigm shift came when an F-117, serial number 82-0806, call sign Vega 31, was shot down by a Soviet-legacy air defense battery. This event remains the first, and to this day only, successful combat shoot-down of a Nighthawk.

The aircraft was piloted by Lieutenant Colonel Dale Zelko, a veteran combat flyer returning from a strike near Belgrade. Repetitive flight routes and complacency were largely attributed to the historic loss. Operating from Aviano Air Base, Italy, the Nighthawk fleet had flown predictable strike corridors into Serbia and underestimated the threat after so many successful sorties.

NATO leaders declined to assign electronic jamming escorts like the Grumman EA-6B Prowler as it was viewed as necessary. Meanwhile, Yugoslav intelligence used airfield spotters to track takeoff times and coordinate with regional commanders to project exactly when the aircraft would enter the airspace near concealed surface-to-air missile batteries.

弗吉尼亚州尚蒂伊史蒂文·F·乌德瓦-哈齐中心的大型博物馆已经拥有无与伦比的藏品，这架标志性的棱角黑色喷气机的到来是一个里程碑式的补充。作为第一架采用真正隐形技术制造的作战飞机，F-117 拉开了低可观测性、反雷达技术的竞赛，该技术定义了现代空战时代。 Overachiever 是一架经过精心设计的机身，拥有辉煌的服役历史，使其成为 Av Geeks 访问该国首都的必看景点。
F-117A 于 1989 年 12 月 19 日在正义事业行动中首次亮相。第 37 战术战斗机联队的六架飞机从内华达州托诺帕起飞，执行需要五次空中加油的远程任务。主要任务是对巴拿马国防军 2000 营所在地里奥哈托机场的基础设施进行打击。策划者的目的是击晕沉睡的驻军，为空袭后美国陆军游骑兵乘运输机低空空投扫清道路。
战术计划要求精确定时，在伞兵到达前30秒引爆常规炸弹。凌晨 1 点 01 分，格雷戈里·费斯特上尉在军营旁边投下一枚 2,000 磅（907 公斤）GBU-27 激光制导炸弹，产生的冲击波震碎了窗户，使当地部队陷入混乱。
最后一刻的目标变化、风向变化和技术错误导致第二架 F-117A 的炸弹偏离目标。这次突然袭击还因一次泄密而受到影响，该泄密使一些国防军部队在袭击前撤离了建筑物。

body_en: Autoflight V5000 Matrix william.moore@… Tue, 03/31/2026 - 07:48 The V5000 Matrix is a lift-plus-cruise hybrid-electric/all-electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft being developed by AutoFlight Europe GmbH. Unveiled in February 2026, the aircraft performed a remotely piloted transition from thrustborne hover to wingborne cruise, demonstrating that flight testing is already underway. It features a long, aerodynamic cabin with panoramic viewing windows and skid-style landing gear. A main high wing is complemented by two smaller wings to the front and rear of the aircraft, with three booms extending across all three wings parallel to the cabin, on each side. 20 two-blade fixed propellers are mounted to the six booms to provide lift, while eight cruise propellers provide forward thrust, four mounted to the front and four to the rear. title_en: Turkey Signs $11 Billion Eurofighter Deal
title_zh: 土耳其签署价值 110 亿美元的欧洲战斗机协议
summary: Turkey Signs $11 Billion Eurofighter Deal hockensmithawi… Mon, 10/27/2025 - 18:19 Turkey has signed a long-anticipated £8 billion ($11 billion) deal to acquire Eurofighter Typhoons, the first major export contract for the four-nation combat aircraft since 2017
summary_zh: 土耳其签署价值 110 亿美元的欧洲战斗机协议 hockensmithawi…
body_en: Turkey Signs $11 Billion Eurofighter Deal hockensmithawi… Mon, 10/27/2025 - 18:19 Turkey has signed a long-anticipated £8 billion ($11 billion) deal to acquire Eurofighter Typhoons, the first major export contract for the four-nation combat aircraft since 2017. Twenty new-built aircraft will be purchased in the country’s first acquisition of a European combat aircraft after decades of operating new and secondhand U.S.-built fighters. But Turkey’s Eurofighter order could more than double in size, according to Turkish Defense Minister Yasar Guler. He declared that Ankara would also buy another 24 aircraft second hand, 12 each from Oman and Qatar. If those sales go through, Oman would be giving up Eurofighter operations. With deliveries of the new-build aircraft not due until 2030, delivering those second-hand aircraft—potentially as early as next year from Qatar, according to Guler—would allow Turkey to accelerate the Eurofighter’s entry into service and enable the retirement of older aircraft from its inventory, including the McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom. BAE Systems, which will produce the newly built aircraft in Warton, England, says it will receive £5.4 billion of the £8 billion deal. Included in the £5.4 billion are the aircraft and the weapons package from MBDA, including some integration work, potentially for Turkish indigenous weaponry. The remaining £2.6 billion is support and training activity, which will be contracted later, BAE Systems officials say. It is unclear whether the deal will ultimately include offsets to enable Turkish industry to become involved in the Eurofighter program and for Turkey to have a level of freedom of action for the fleet. After decades of facing numerous arms embargoes, Turkey often demands the ability to locally perform airframe, system and engine maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) in-country. The deal was struck during a meeting between UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in Ankara. Starmer said the deal was a win for British workers and the wider UK defense industry. Government officials claim the order is “saving the Warton production line,” after concerns about a lack of new orders for UK-built Typhoons were expressed by workers unions. UK industry has a 37% share in the Eurofighter program and production of major component assemblies is being ramped up thanks to orders from the other Eurofighter partner nations including Germany, Italy and Spain. “Today’s announcement extends Typhoon production and preserves crucial sovereign skills which underpin the UK’s defense and security,” BAE Systems CEO Charles Woodburn said. The deal is another major boost for the UK defense industry, coming just weeks after the UK’s Type 26 frigates were selected by Norway in a £10 billion deal. UK Defense Secretary John Healey said the deal went beyond the procurement of aircraft. “It is the leading edge of the growing defense and industrial partnership between our two nations,” he said. As part of the visit, Starmer also visited the facilities of Turkish Aerospace Industries, where he was shown the indigenous Kaan combat aircraft. He was also exposed to the Hurjet advanced jet trainer, a potential candidate to replace the BAE Systems Hawk jet trainer in the UK Royal Air Force (RAF) inventory. The deal follows three years of negotiations, which have included lobbying of the German government for Berlin to lift a restriction on a Eurofighter sale after Erdoğan’s government arrested Istanbul Mayor Ekrem İmamoğlu, who is seen as a serious presidential rival to Erdoğan in upcoming elections. The administration of German Chancellor Friedrich Merz lifted the sanctions in part because of the benefit to German industry. A memorandum of understanding between the UK and Turkish governments for a Eurofighter sale was agreed to in July. Turkey’s interest in the aircraft is driven in part by a need for a more capable air combat platform to be available in the interim until advanced versions of the Kaan aircraft are produced in the 2030s. Ankara’s decision to opt for a European fighter, meanwhile, will have been driven by a need to diversify sources of supply after facing sanctions from the U.S. over its purchase of a Russian air defense system and banishment from the F-35 Joint Strike Fighter program. The transfer of Omani and Qatari aircraft to Turkey begs questions over the future of additional Eurofighter orders from Qatar, which has long been linked to orders for a further 12 aircraft for a total of 36. Oman, meanwhile, appears to want to consolidate its fighter fleet around the Lockheed Martin F-16 Block 50. In BAE Systems’ 2023 full-year results, the company revealed that the Omani air force had chosen not to renew support arrangements for its Typhoons, and it is unclear how active that fleet now is. Buying these additional aircraft would mean Turkey would have a mix of three configurations in its fleet. Qatar’s aircraft have the Mk.0 version of the active electronically scanned array European Common Radar System (ECRS) radar, while Oman’s feature the mechanically scanned Captor sensor. In addition to the Eurofighter order, Erdoğan and Starmer also revealed they were working on a new trade and security pact. body_en: Project Lotus, Northrop Grumman’s Secret Autonomous Aircraft Revealed hockensmithawi… Mon, 10/27/2025 - 18:05 Northrop Grumman has secretly built a large new uncrewed aircraft system (UAS), dubbed Project Lotus, at the company’s Scaled Composites rapid prototyping facility in Mojave, California, a source familiar with the project tells Aviation Week. A photo of the aircraft reviewed by Aviation Week revealed a completed, turbofan-powered aircraft parked within the Scaled Composites compound at the public airport. The Lotus UAS design in some ways resembles features of the newly revealed Lockheed Martin Project Vectis, with a long, slender fuselage positioned forward of the leading edges of the wings, capped by a nose with swept-back edges leading to a slender point. In many other respects, the Lotus and Vectis designs diverge. Unlike the engine inlet mounted low at mid-fuselage for the Vectis aircraft, the Lotus inlet sits high atop of the extreme aft section of its fuselage. The Lotus also sports sharply canted tails, breaking from the tailless-configured Vectis. Project Lotus appears to represent Northrop’s candidate for the U.S. Air Force’s Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) Increment 2 program, which is finalizing requirements for competitive prototypes ahead of a scheduled acquisition process next year. The photo reveals that Northrop has already built a demonstrator, perhaps gaining a step on Lockheed’s rival design, which is not scheduled to reach first flight until 2027. As Northrop’s rapid prototyping arm, the Scaled Composites facility frequently builds aircraft demonstrators in secret. Scaled Composites registered a turbofan-powered, fixed-wing aircraft identified only as Model 444 earlier this year with the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), which granted the organization the N444LX tail number. It is not clear if the registration represents Project Lotus or another undisclosed project. Northrop also is building the XRQ-73, also known as the Series Hybrid Electric Propulsion AiR Demonstration (Shepard), for DARPA. In response to questions about Project Lotus from Aviation Week, Northrop avoided direct answers, but spoke generally about its internal investments in autonomous aircraft. “Our investments prioritize production at speed and scale, without sacrificing performance or capability. The Northrop Grumman team has generated step-change advancements in production speed, weight and parts reduction, and overall cost efficiency. These advancements benefit the spectrum of autonomous capabilities we produce at Northrop Grumman for U.S. and international customers,” Northrop said. As Lockheed’s Project Vectis design revealed in September, Northrop’s Project Lotus represents one side in a long-running debate within industry and the Air Force over the future direction of the CCA fleet between concepts that emphasize greater survivability or lower cost. In 2024, the Air Force decided to seek a middle ground between cost and survivability with the selected competitive prototypes for the CCA Increment 1 program. The General Atomics Aeronautical Systems Inc. YFQ-42 and Anduril YFQ-44 are large aircraft that feature some low-observable, or stealth, technology. But the aircraft are larger and costlier than, for example, the Kratos XQ-58, and lack the stealthier features of Project Vectis and Project Lotus. In September, Air Force officials said they were considering the full spectrum of options for the Increment 2 CCA requirement, ranging from exquisite survivability to small, air-launched systems. Project Lotus also lends new insight into how Northrop’s internal CCA concepts have evolved from previous, publicly released ideas. As the Air Force competition for CCAs heated up in 2023, Northrop showed off the SG-1 and SG-2 concepts, which appeared similar to the cranked-kite planform of the U.S. Navy-funded X-47B demonstrator. Around the same time, Northrop also unveiled the Model 437 concept, an autonomous spinoff from the crewed Model 401 Sierra demonstrator. The Model 437 finally emerged as a piloted demonstrator aircraft in 2024. Earlier this year, Northrop announced that the aircraft had transitioned into the Beacon demonstrator, serving as a testbed for mission autonomy technology. The milestone comes nearly 22 months after Northrop completed the maiden sortie of the first flight test version of the B-21 on Nov. 10, 2023. The company has also delivered to the Air Force two more fully assembled airframes, which are reserved for static and fatigue testing on the ground. title_en: Delta Ran Icelandair Out Of Detroit, Then Cut The Route Itself: The Nasty Side Of Competition
title_zh: 达美航空将冰岛航空从底特律撤出，然后又自行削减航线：竞争的令人讨厌的一面
summary: Icelandair launched Detroit to Keflavik in 2023, Delta matched it, Icelandair left, and now Delta has cut the route too. Detroit is back to zero Iceland flights.
summary_zh: 冰岛航空于2023年开通了底特律飞往凯夫拉维克的航线，达美航空也跟进了，冰岛航空离开了，现在达美航空也削减了这条航线。底特律回到零 Icela
body_en: Usually we say that competition is good for consumers, but here’s a case where it isn’t, as a Delta hub will go from having two airlines flying to Iceland, to having zero airlines flying to Iceland. I guess there’s no one to really blame here, but it’s bad for consumers!
Delta cuts Detroit to Keflavik route, after Icelandair exit

Icelandair operates a unique business model, whereby it uses its hub in Keflavik (KEF) to serve markets on both sides of the Atlantic, so that the airline can tap into the local market, as well as offer one-stop service all over the place.

In 2023, we saw Icelandair launch flights to Detroit (DTW) . Detroit is a fortress hub for Delta, so the airline has a lot of pricing power there. Of course Icelandair’s idea was to undercut the major players on pricing, while also giving travelers the opportunity of a stopover in Iceland.

As you’d expect, airlines tend to defend their hubs, so less than two weeks after Icelandair’s announcement, Delta announced it would launch exactly the same route , and would even start the service three days earlier. This was obviously not a coincidence, but a competitive response.

Admittedly I suspect Icelandair had to know that Delta might replicate its route, and that proved to be too much competition. In early 2026, Icelandair fully ended Detroit service, as it couldn’t make the math work. Well, at least consumers would still have one option to Iceland, right? Not so fast, unfortunately.
Delta has now also quietly pulled the Detroit to Keflavik route, instead choosing to launch service to Iceland out of Boston (BOS). So yeah, now Detroit is back to having zero Iceland flights.
I guess that’s just how competition works, right?
Obviously this is a case where consumers initially won by having two players, but then eventually lost, by having no remaining service. This is the downside to competition.

Obviously Delta wasn’t looking out for consumers here, but the company was looking out for its bottom line. Airlines fiercely defend their hubs, so I guess this was the inevitable outcome, when you think about it. Delta wasn’t going to let Icelandair launch this route without matching it. And then when Icelandair left as a competitor, it’s also not surprising Delta cut the route, because if it wanted to operate the service in the first place, it would’ve done so before Icelandair.

I can’t help but wonder if Delta’s Minneapolis (MSP) to Dublin (DUB) route will have a similar fare. Aer Lingus added service in the market in 2024, and Delta immediately matched. Aer Lingus is ending this route with the close of the 2026 season. Will this route survive for Delta beyond 2027? We’ll see, I guess!

Icelandair starting flying from Keflavik to Detroit, and Delta immediately matched. Icelandair then pulled out of the market, and then Delta also immediately matched. Going from zero competitors to two competitors to zero competitors isn’t exactly ideal for consumers, but often it’s how these situations play out, unfortunately.
What do you make of this Detroit to Keflavik competitive situation?
body_zh: 通常我们说竞争对消费者有利，但这里的情况却并非如此，因为达美航空枢纽将从拥有两家飞往冰岛的航空公司变成拥有零家飞往冰岛的航空公司。我想这并不能怪罪任何人，但这对消费者来说是不利的！
冰岛航空退出后，达美航空削减了底特律至凯夫拉维克的航线
冰岛航空采用独特的商业模式，利用凯夫拉维克枢纽（KEF）服务大西洋两岸市场，既能开拓当地市场，又能提供遍布各地的一站式服务。
2023 年，冰岛航空开通了飞往底特律 (DTW) 的航班。底特律是达美航空的要塞枢纽，因此该航空公司在那里拥有很大的定价权。当然，冰岛航空的想法是在价格上低于主要参与者，同时也为旅行者提供在冰岛中途停留的机会。
正如你所料，航空公司倾向于保卫自己的枢纽，因此在冰岛航空宣布这一消息后不到两周，达美航空就宣布将推出完全相同的航线，甚至提前三天开始服务。这显然不是巧合，而是一种竞争反应。
诚然，我怀疑冰岛航空必须知道达美航空可能会复制其航线，而事实证明这竞争太激烈了。 2026 年初，冰岛航空全面终止了底特律航班服务，因为它无法进行数学计算。好吧，至少消费者还有冰岛的一种选择，对吧？不幸的是，没那么快。
达美航空现在也悄悄取消了底特律至凯夫拉维克的航线，转而选择开通从波士顿 (BOS) 飞往冰岛的航班。所以，是的，现在底特律又恢复了零冰岛航班。
我想这就是竞争的方式，对吗？
显然，在这种情况下，消费者最初因拥有两名玩家而获胜，但最终因没有剩余服务而失败。这是竞争的缺点。
显然，达美航空并没有在这里关注消费者，但该公司正在关注其利润。航空公司会极力保卫自己的枢纽机场，所以仔细想想，我想这是不可避免的结果。达美航空不会让冰岛航空在没有与之匹配的情况下开通这条航线。然后，当冰岛航空作为竞争对手离开时，达美航空削减这条航线也就不足为奇了，因为如果它想首先运营这项服务，它就会在冰岛航空之前这样做。
我不禁想知道达美航空的明尼阿波利斯 (MSP) 至都柏林 (DUB) 航线是否会有类似的票价。爱尔兰航空于 2024 年在市场上增加了服务，达美航空立即跟进。爱尔兰航空将在 2026 赛季结束时结束这条航线。达美航空的这条航线在 2027 年之后还能继续存在吗？我想我们会看到的！
冰岛航空开始从凯夫拉维克飞往底特律的航班，达美航空立即跟进。冰岛航空随后退出市场，随后达美航空也立即跟进。从零个竞争对手到两个竞争对手再到零个竞争对手对于消费者来说并不完全理想，但不幸的是，这些情况往往就是这样发生的。
您如何看待底特律到凯夫拉维克的竞争形势？

title_en: Lufthansa Loses Greenwashing Lawsuit, Rebrands Green Fares As Impact Fares
title_zh: 汉莎航空败诉绿色清洗诉讼，将绿色票价重新命名为影响力票价
summary: Lufthansa is renaming its Green Fares to Impact Fares after losing a greenwashing lawsuit brought by Environmental Action Germany. Here's what's changing and what stays the same.
summary_zh: 在德国环境行动组织提起的绿色清洗诉讼败诉后，汉莎航空将其绿色票价更名为影响票价。这是变化的
body_en: In 2023, Lufthansa introduced “Green Fares.” As you may have guessed based on the name, the idea is that these fares offer some level of carbon offsets, but beyond that, they offer added flexibility, plus bonus miles and status qualification. Well, Lufthansa has now announced that it’s rebranding these fares , and the change isn’t voluntary…
Lufthansa Group is renaming its Green Fares, and going forward, they’ll be known as Impact Fares. Here’s how Lufthansa describes this change:

The Lufthansa Group is renaming its Green Fare to Impact Fare. The new name places even stronger emphasis on customers’ contribution to greater sustainability in aviation and thus reflects new regulatory requirements for environmental communication: By choosing an Impact Fare, passengers support the additional use of Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) across the Lufthansa Group’s route network. In addition, they contribute to selected climate protection projects outside the company’s value chain.

Lufthansa explains that for every Impact Fare booked, the company deploys an additional amount of sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) in its flight operation within six months of departure. For flights within Europe, this volume is based on 20% of the estimated flight related CO2 emissions.

The fare also supports climate protection projects, based on the remaining 80% of the estimated flight related CO2 emissions. On intercontinental routes, the ratio is 10% to 90%. In addition, passengers receive bonus miles for these fares, along with more flexible rebooking options.
Lufthansa lost a court battle over these Green Fares

While Lufthansa acknowledges that the rebranding of these fares is in response to “new regulatory requirements,” the airline also tries to claim that “the new name places even stronger emphasis on customers’ contribution to greater sustainability in aviation.”

So, what’s really going on here? In March 2025, NGO Environmental Action Germany won a greenwashing lawsuit against Lufthansa related to these fares, on grounds of misleading consumers with sustainability claims. The court had ruled that consumers choosing to offset their flights with the “Green Fares” were left in the dark as to the extent of the carrier’s climate compensation in relation to the flight booked. Furthermore, the fares including SAF made it seem like consumers were directly contributing to offsetting their own flights.

As the NGO Environmental Action Germany explained, “the court confirms our criticism and addresses how one of the world’s largest airlines systematically deceives customers and pretends that air travel is climate-neutral in exchange for additional fees.”

Now, at this point that was over 18 months ago, but as you’d expect, it often takes time for cases to go through courts, appeals to happen, etc. So we’re just now seeing the impact of this lawsuit, and Lufthansa finally making the change. There is a certain irony to Lufthansa losing a battle for greenwashing, and then claiming the new name places an even stronger emphasis on how much customers are contributing to sustainability. Hmmm…

This isn’t the first time that Lufthansa has gotten in trouble for greenwashing. In 2022, Lufthansa got in trouble with UK regulators over an ad that showed a plane in the top half of the image, and the earth in the bottom half of the image, with the following caption:
“LUFTHANSA GROUP, CONNECTING THE WORLD. PROTECTING ITS FUTURE. #MakeChangeFly”

Lufthansa is once again in trouble for greenwashing. This time around, the airline has been forced to rebrand its Green Fares, with the claim being that they made consumers believe that by booking these fares, they weren’t harming the environment. These fares are now known as Impact Fares, with all the same perks as the previous Green Fares.
What do you make of Lufthansa being forced to rebrand Green Fares?
body_zh: 2023 年，汉莎航空推出“绿色票价”。正如您可能根据名称猜到的那样，这些票价提供了一定程度的碳抵消，但除此之外，它们还提供了更大的灵活性，以及​​奖励里程和身份资格。嗯，汉莎航空现在宣布正在重新命名这些票价，而且这种变化不是自愿的……
汉莎航空集团正在重新命名其绿色票价，今后将更名为“Impact 票价”。汉莎航空是这样描述这一变化的：
汉莎航空集团将其绿色票价更名为影响票价。新名称更加强调客户对航空业可持续发展的贡献，从而反映了环境沟通的新监管要求：通过选择影响票价，乘客支持在汉莎航空集团的航线网络中额外使用可持续航空燃料 (SAF)。此外，他们还为公司价值链之外的选定气候保护项目做出贡献。
汉莎航空解释说，对于预订的每笔影响票价，该公司都会在出发后六个月内在航班运营中额外部署可持续航空燃料 (SAF)。对于欧洲境内的航班，该排放量基于预计航班相关二氧化碳排放量的 20%。
该票价还支持气候保护项目，该项目基于预计飞行相关二氧化碳排放量的剩余 80%。在洲际航线上，这一比例为10%至90%。此外，乘客还可以通过这些票价获得奖励里程，以及更灵活的重新预订选项。
汉莎航空在绿色票价诉讼中败诉
虽然汉莎航空承认这些票价的品牌重塑是为了响应“新的监管要求”，但该航空公司还试图声称“新名称更加强调客户对航空业可持续发展的贡献。”
那么，这里到底发生了什么？ 2025 年 3 月，非政府组织德国环境行动赢得了针对汉莎航空的与这些票价相关的绿色清洗诉讼，理由是其可持续发展声明误导了消费者。法院裁定，选择用“绿色票价”抵消航班的消费者对航空公司与预订航班相关的气候补偿程度一无所知。此外，包括 SAF 在内的票价让人感觉消费者直接为抵消自己的航班做出了贡献。
正如非政府组织德国环境行动所解释的那样，“法院证实了我们的批评，并解决了世界上最大的航空公司之一如何系统性地欺骗客户并假装航空旅行是气候中性的以换取额外费用。”
现在，已经是 18 个月前的事了，但正如您所料，案件通常需要时间经过法院、上诉等。所以我们现在才看到这起诉讼的影响，汉莎航空终于做出了改变。汉莎航空在一场“绿色清洗”斗争中失败，然后声称新名称更加强调客户为可持续发展做出了多少贡献，这颇具讽刺意味。嗯……
这并不是汉莎航空第一次因“漂绿”而陷入麻烦。 2022 年，汉莎航空因一则广告而与英国监管机构发生纠纷，该广告在图像的上半部分显示了一架飞机，在图像的下半部分显示了地球，并附有以下标题：
“汉莎集团，连接世界。保护未来。#MakeChangeFly”
汉莎航空再次陷入绿色清洗的困境。这一次，该航空公司被迫重新命名其绿色票价，声称他们让消费者相信，通过预订这些票价，他们不会损害环境。这些票价现在被称为 Impact 票价，具有与之前的 Green 票价相同的所有福利。
您对汉莎航空被迫重新命名绿色票价有何看法？

title_en: $99 Alaska Companion Fare: How This Atmos Rewards Card Perk Works
title_zh: 99 美元的阿拉斯加同伴票价：Atmos 奖励卡福利如何运作
summary: Atmos Rewards credit cards offer a $99 companion fare for Alaska and Hawaiian flights. Here's how to earn it, redeem it, upgrade it, and get the most value.
summary_zh: Atmos Rewards 信用卡为阿拉斯加和夏威夷航班提供 99 美元的陪伴票价。以下是如何赚取、兑换、升级以及获得最大收益的方法
body_en: There are various airline credit cards that offer some sort of a companion ticket for spending a certain amount. To me, one of the more valuable companion tickets is the one offered by Alaska Air Group, valid for flights on Alaska and Hawaiian.

In this post, I’d like to take a look at the $99 companion fare offered by Atmos Rewards credit cards in more detail, to discuss how it works, and how you can maximize value with it. We’ve seen some rule changes to these over time, so I think it’s worth covering the current state of them.
Link: Learn more about the Atmos™ Rewards Ascent Visa Signature® credit card or Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card
How to earn Alaska & Hawaiian $99 companion fare

There are two credit cards that offer the Alaska and Hawaiian $99 companion fare. Both the Atmos™ Rewards Ascent Visa Signature® credit card ( learn more ) and Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card ( learn more ) offer a $99 companion fare (plus taxes and fees starting from $23).
The idea is that you can book the primary traveler at the standard fare, and then the second passenger will cost you $99, plus any government taxes and fees.
The $99 companion fare is offered as part of the welcome bonuses on these cards. For context, here are the current bonuses available on the card:

The Atmos Rewards Ascent Card is offering a huge welcome bonus of up to 80,000 points plus a $99 companion fare (plus taxes and fees from $23); earn 60,000 points plus the companion fare after spending $3,000 within the first 90 days, and earn an additional 20,000 points after spending a total of $5,000 within the same period
The Atmos Rewards Business Card is offering 70,000 points plus a $99 companion fare (plus taxes and fees from $23) after spending $4,000 within the first 90 days

On top of that, you can earn a $99 companion fare each anniversary year if you spend $6,000 on the card. Keep in mind that you’re potentially eligible for both of these cards (including the welcome bonuses), so it’s possible to earn multiple certificates.

There’s merit to picking up both the personal card and business card, given their low fees and useful benefits. For that matter, if you’re a household with four or more people, it could also make sense for you and your spouse to each get one of these cards, so that you could use two companion certificates for a total of four passengers.

You’ll find that your $99 companion fare is deposited in your Atmos Rewards account shortly after you reach the minimum spending requirement in the first year, and shortly after your account anniversary in subsequent years (assuming you reach the spending requirement). The terms state that it could take up to two billing cycles, but in my experience, it typically posts much faster than that.

Let me also emphasize that these $99 companion fares are separate from the Global Companion Awards (worth 25,000 points or 100,000 points) that can be earned with the Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite ® Credit Card ( learn more ), which can be used when redeeming Atmos Rewards points . There’s a huge incentive to spend money on that card, given all the great perks offered .
How to redeem Alaska & Hawaiian $99 companion fare
When it comes to redeeming the Alaska and Hawaiian $99 companion fare, there are some details to be aware of, as you’d expect:

The $99 companion fare is valid for travel on Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines within the Americas, including for travel in the state of Hawaii; however, it’s not valid for travel to Pacific destinations outside the United States, to Europe, etc.
The $99 companion fare is only valid for tickets booked in economy, though all economy fare classes are included
The $99 companion fare can only be used when there are exactly two people on a reservation, so if you have a reservation with more than two people, the option to use it won’t show

Tickets booked with the $99 companion fare are upgradeable, both for the primary passenger and companion (this includes using complimentary elite upgrades, upgrade certificates, instant upgrade fares, etc.)
Both passengers booked with the $99 companion fare earn points for their tickets, whether crediting to Atmos Rewards or a partner program

title_en: Is InterContinental Ambassador Status Worth It? Benefits & Cost Explained
title_zh: 洲际大使身份值得吗？效益和成本解释
summary: InterContinental Ambassador is a paid program separate from IHG One Rewards. Here's what it costs, what perks you get, and why it's probably worth it for frequent InterContinental guests.
summary_zh: 洲际大使是一项独立于 IHG One Rewards 的付费计划。以下是它的成本、您获得的福利以及为什么它可能值得
body_en: While IHG One Rewards is the loyalty program for InterContinental Hotels Group (IHG), there’s separately the InterContinental Ambassador program (sometimes referred to as IHG Ambassador, though it is InterContinental specific). This can cause some confusion, since often people don’t really get the distinction between IHG One Rewards and InterContinental Ambassador. In this post, I’d like to take a closer look at that.

The InterContinental Ambassador program is a paid guest recognition program intended specifically for frequent guests of InterContinental hotels. InterContinental is one of IHG’s premium hotel brands, and if you stay at InterContinentals with any frequency, then a membership should pay for itself.

This status is separate from IHG One Rewards Platinum and IHG One Rewards Diamond status , so it could make sense to buy into this program even if you have those status levels. Similarly, qualifying for IHG One Rewards Milestone Rewards is independent of the perks offered to Ambassador members.

So the idea is that Ambassador offers perks at InterContinental properties (as well as select Six Senses properties), while it doesn’t offer direct perks at other brands (well, other than that it offers IHG Platinum status, which does offer perks). If you don’t specifically stay at InterContinental or Six Senses properties with any frequency, then this isn’t going to be worth considering.
How much does InterContinental Ambassador cost?

InterContinental Ambassador is purely a paid program. Any IHG One Rewards member can buy a 12-month Ambassador membership for either $225 or 45,000 IHG One Rewards points. Based on my latest miles & points valuations , IHG points are worth 0.5 cents each, so to me it’s breakeven whether it makes sense to pay with points or cash (in which case I’d pay with points).

The 12-month membership year doesn’t have to coincide with the calendar year, so I’d only recommend signing up shortly before your first planned stay. Note that sometimes there are also promotions for new InterContinental Ambassador members, in which case it could make sense to sign up then.
You can register for the InterContinental Ambassador program online, by phone via the Ambassador service center, or at an IHG hotel.
What benefits does InterContinental Ambassador offer?
What are the benefits of InterContinental Ambassador status? When staying at InterContinental hotels, you receive the following perks:
Complimentary weekend night reward; I’ll share more details on that below
A guaranteed one category upgrade; this excludes club access and certain suite types, and isn’t guaranteed on award stays
A $20 credit with each stay to use toward the hotel’s restaurant, bar, or minibar
Guaranteed 4PM late check-out; this applies at both city hotels and resorts

IHG One Rewards Platinum status , which offers 60% bonus points, upgrades subject to availability, rollover elite nights, and more; you also receive this status just for having The Brand New IHG One Rewards Premier Select Credit Card ( learn more ), The New IHG One Rewards Business Credit Card ( learn more ), Chase Sapphire Reserve® Card ( learn more ), Sapphire Reserve for Business℠ ( learn more ), or United Club℠ Card ( learn more )
Exclusively in Mainland China, complimentary full breakfast each night valid only for the member (so one person per room)
I think most of these benefits are pretty straightforward. I’d say the complimentary weekend night reward is potentially the highest value perk here. For those curious about how that works:

It’s valid for 12 months from the date of issue, and it’s issued as soon as you sign up for the program (or renew); if you sign up for the program at check-in of a stay, you could then use it for that stay

It’s valid for a minimum of a two night paid weekend stay, using the Ambassador Complimentary Weekend Night Rate at any InterContinental property (this will show as “AMB Certificate” when booking); so it’s not valid when redeeming points, or booking other rates
Weekend nights are defined as Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, except in the Middle East, where hotels may define the weekend as Thursday, Friday, and Saturday

title_en: Buy GHA Discovery Dollars (D$) For 15% Off: Intriguing, But Is It Worth It?
title_zh: 购买 GHA Discovery Dollars (D$) 享受 15% 折扣：很有趣，但值得吗？
summary: GHA Discovery is selling Discovery Dollars (D$) at 15% off through November 19, 2026. Here's how the deal works and the catch that shrinks the real savings.
summary_zh: GHA Discovery 正在以 15% 的折扣出售 Discovery Dollars (D$)，截止日期为 2026 年 11 月 19 日。以下是该交易的运作方式以及缩小真实销售额的问题
body_en: Global Hotel Alliance (GHA) is an alliance of (mostly small) hotel groups that don’t otherwise belong to major hotel loyalty programs, and GHA Discovery is the loyalty program of these hotels .

It’s a fascinating loyalty program for some really stellar brands, like Capella Hotels & Resorts . There’s also often a status match promotion , which is an easy way to elevate your stays with eligible brands. If you want to get as much value from your stays as possible, GHA has just rolled out an interesting promotion… is it worth it, though?
Get a deal on GHA stays by buying D$ at a discount

Between October 22 and November 19, 2026, GHA Discovery is offering 15% off the purchase of Discovery Dollars (D$) , the program’s rewards currency. The idea is that you can buy each D$ for 0.85 USD, and you can purchase up to 5,000 D$ with this offer.

D$ expire 24 months after they’re issued, and can’t be extended, even with activity. They can be redeemed toward most charges at most hotels, at the rate of one D$ per USD. The only things that generally aren’t eligible for redemption are taxes, tips, fees, etc. Also keep in mind that you don’t earn D$ on any portion of your stay for which you redeem D$.

So essentially think of this as an opportunity to save 15% on a GHA stay, which seems pretty compelling, assuming you have firm plans to make a stay in the near future. However, is it really worth it?
The catch with the GHA Discovery D$ promotion
GHA Discovery is a revenue based loyalty program, so there aren’t any arbitrage opportunities that will get you more value. Still, 15% off a hotel stay sounds good… right?

Yes, I would say it’s mostly a good deal, but the catch is that when you redeem D$, you don’t earn rewards for that portion of the stay. Ordinarily, GHA Discovery members earn anywhere from 4-7% back on their stays (in the form of D$), so you’re forgoing a 4-7% return in order to save 15%. That still leaves you with an 8-11% spread. However:
GHA Discovery sometimes has promotions offering bonus D$ for stays, so you’re also forgoing that

Purchasing D$ doesn’t code as hotel spending on credit cards, but instead, codes as “other services,” and that means you’re potentially forgoing quite some points there ; for example, I earn 4x points on hotel spending with my credit cards, while I “only” earn 2x points on everyday spending

So I think for some people, the math could work out nicely. Like, if you have an upcoming $5,000 Capella stay, then saving $750 on that sounds great. However, it’s not necessarily as much of a slam dunk as you might assume at first glance, when you consider the things you’re forgoing.

GHA is selling Discovery Dollars (D$) for 15% off, which is an opportunity to get a discount on a stay with dozens of different hotel brands, including ones like Anantara, Capella, Kempinski, Pan Pacific, Patina, and more.

Being able to essentially buy a discount on a hotel stay could be a good value, but the catch is that you don’t earn rewards on the portion of the stay you redeem for, and buying Discovery Dollars also doesn’t code as hotel spending for credit cards.

Given that you usually earn a 4-7% return on GHA spending, that lowers the real value here to 8-11%, before any additional promotions, and that doesn’t factor in the possible difference in credit card rewards. So I think this could make sense with an upcoming stay, but it’s not any sort of slam dunk.
body_zh: 全球酒店联盟 (GHA) 是一个由不属于主要酒店忠诚度计划的酒店集团（大多数是小型）组成的联盟，而 GHA Discovery 是这些酒店的忠诚度计划。
对于嘉佩乐酒店及度假村等一些真正的明星品牌来说，这是一项令人着迷的忠诚度计划。通常还会有身份匹配促销活动，这是提升您在符合条件的品牌中的停留时间的简单方法。如果您想从住宿中获得尽可能多的价值，GHA 刚刚推出了一项有趣的促销活动……但值得吗？
以折扣价购买 D$，获得 GHA 住宿优惠
2026 年 10 月 22 日至 11 月 19 日期间，GHA Discovery 提供购买该计划奖励货币 Discovery Dollars (D$) 的 15% 折扣。这个想法是，您可以以 0.85 美元的价格购买每个 D$，并且通过此优惠您最多可以购买 5,000 D$。
D$ 在发行后 24 个月后到期，并且即使有活动也无法延期。它们可以在大多数酒店兑换大部分费用，汇率为 1 美元兑换 1 美元。通常唯一不符合兑换资格的项目是税费、小费、费用等。另请注意，您在兑换 D$ 的住宿期间的任何部分都无法赚取 D$。
因此，本质上可以将此视为在 GHA 住宿上节省 15% 的机会，假设您有在不久的将来入住的明确计划，这似乎相当有吸引力。然而，这真的值得吗？
GHA Discovery D$ 促销活动的亮点
GHA Discovery 是一项基于收入的忠诚度计划，因此不存在任何可以为您带来更多价值的套利机会。不过，酒店住宿 15% 的折扣听起来不错……对吗？
是的，我想说这基本上是一笔不错的交易，但问题是，当您兑换 D$ 时，您不会获得该部分住宿的奖励。通常，GHA Discovery 会员在住宿期间可赚取 4-7% 的返利（以 D 美元的形式），因此您需要放弃 4-7% 的返利才能节省 15%。这仍然给你留下 8-11% 的价差。然而：
GHA Discovery 有时会举办促销活动，为住宿提供奖金 D$，所以您也可以放弃这一点
购买 D$ 并不编码为信用卡上的酒店消费，而是编码为“其他服务”，这意味着您可能会放弃相当多的积分；例如，我使用信用卡在酒店消费可赚取 4 倍积分，而日常消费“仅”可赚取 2 倍积分
所以我认为对于某些人来说，数学可以很好地解决问题。例如，如果您即将入住 5,000 美元的 Capella 住宿，那么节省 750 美元听起来很棒。然而，当你考虑到你要放弃的东西时，它并不一定像你乍一看想象的那么扣篮。
GHA 正在以 15% 的折扣出售 Discovery Dollars (D$)，这是在数十个不同酒店品牌住宿时获得折扣的机会，包括 Anantara、Capella、Kempinski、Pan Pacific、Patina 等。
能够以折扣价购买酒店住宿可能很划算，但问题是您兑换的住宿部分无法获得奖励，而且购买 Discovery Dollars 也不算是信用卡的酒店消费。
鉴于您通常会获得 4-7% 的 GHA 支出回报，在任何额外促销之前，这会将实际价值降低至 8-11%，并且这还不考虑信用卡奖励可能存在的差异。所以我认为这对于即将到来的住宿来说可能是有意义的，但这并不是任何形式的灌篮。

Romanian carrier seeks protection from creditors as total liabilities reach €25.4 million; flight operations face uncertainty

Romanian airline Dan Air has filed for insolvency proceedings at the Ilfov Tribunal, citing mounting financial pressure and an approximately €10 million debt owed to Romania’s Environmental Fund Administration (AFM).
The application was submitted on 22 October 2026, making Dan Air the second Romanian airline to seek insolvency protection in recent weeks, following similar developments involving AnimaWings.
According to Romanian media reports, Dan Air’s total liabilities reached RON 126.3 million (€25.4 million) at the end of 2025, up from approximately RON 90.2 million (€18.1 million) a year earlier.
Dan Air chief executive Matt Ian David said the insolvency application was intended to protect the airline from enforcement proceedings over a debt of approximately €10 million owed to the AFM.
The obligation relates to carbon emissions allowances required under environmental regulations applicable to airlines.
David said the company had discussed the situation with its aircraft lessors and other business partners, adding that agreements had been reached to support continued operations.

He attributed the airline’s financial difficulties in part to soaring fuel costs, explaining that the company had prioritised purchasing fuel to operate scheduled flights rather than settling the outstanding environmental obligations.
Despite initially stating that the insolvency filing would not affect its flight schedule, Dan Air subsequently suspended its flights, according to Romanian media reports.

The airline indicated that it intended to resume operations from 25 October under a revised schedule. The resumption and the status of individual flights remain subject to confirmation by the carrier.
Passengers booked on Dan Air services should check directly with the airline for the latest information regarding cancellations, rescheduled departures and possible refunds.
Insolvency does not automatically mean bankruptcy

The filing of an insolvency application does not, by itself, mean that a company has entered liquidation or that it must immediately cease trading. The court must first decide whether to open proceedings.

Dan Air’s application seeks protection from creditors and the opportunity to address its financial obligations. The outcome will depend on the court’s decision and the company’s ability to maintain operations while dealing with its liabilities.

Founded in 2017, Dan Air operates scheduled services from Romania, including routes associated with Bucharest and Bac?u airports. The airline previously operated scheduled flights from Bra?ov-Ghimbav International Airport before moving its main operating base to Bac?u.
Dan Air’s financial difficulties follow the recent insolvency proceedings involving AnimaWings, highlighting mounting pressure on parts of Romania’s aviation sector.

该义务涉及适用于航空公司的环境法规所要求的碳排放配额。
大卫表示，该公司已与飞机租赁商和其他业务合作伙伴讨论了这一情况，并补充说已达成协议以支持持续运营。
他将该航空公司的财务困难部分归因于燃油成本飙升，并解释说该公司优先考虑购买燃油来运营定期航班，而不是解决未履行的环境义务。

该航空公司表示，打算根据修订后的时间表从 10 月 25 日起恢复运营。个别航班的恢复和状态仍有待航空公司确认。

title_en: American Airlines’ Most Senior Flight Attendant Retires After 63+ Years
title_zh: 美国航空最资深空乘人员在工作 63 多年后退休
summary: Carol Fair, American's most senior active flight attendant, retires October 26, 2026 after more than 63 years, taking her final flight from London to Charlotte at age 83.
summary_zh: 美国航空界最资深的现役空乘人员卡罗尔·费尔 (Carol Fair) 于 2026 年 10 月 26 日退休，工作了 63 多年，她将乘坐最后一次航班从伦敦飞往
body_en: In the United States, it’s common to find flight attendants of all ages. There’s no maximum age to work as a flight attendant, as long as you can pass your recurrent training each year. The system also greatly incentivizes sticking around when you’re senior, since you’re maxed out on pay, and get your choice of routes, given seniority based bidding.
Along those lines, American’s current most senior flight attendant is about to retire, and I think that makes for an interesting story.
83-year-old American flight attendant retires after 63+ years

Ted Reed has the story of how American Airlines’ most senior flight attendant, Carol Fair, will be retiring on Monday, October 26, 2026, as she takes her last flight from London (LHR) to Charlotte (CLT). The 83-year-old first started her career in 1963 at Piedmont Airlines, before working at US Airways, and then American (given all the mergers). So she’ll be retiring after a career of over 63 years.

Fair is retiring as the number one active flight attendant on American’s seniority list, which includes around 30,000 people. Technically she’s only the third most senior flight attendant at the airline, but the two most senior no longer fly, but haven’t officially retired. Funny enough, when Fair first started her career, she was rejected at American, as the airline claimed she “wasn’t American material.” However, two mergers later, she landed at the airline she hoped to work for in the first place.

The airline is expected to have a water salute for Fair upon landing in Charlotte on Monday, an honor that’s typically reserved for pilots on their last flight, and not flight attendants. As Fair looks back on her career, she shared the following:
“It’s time. I’ve enjoyed every minute of it. I made No. 1 out of 30,000. You can’t go any higher, so I might as well hang it up.”

As you’d expect, Fair primarily flies internationally, given that it’s the easiest way to rack up a lot of hours, and minimize the number of days you have to work. She also explained that she prefers the quality of passengers to those on domestic flights, saying “they are vented better.” Hah.
American’s most senior flight attendant had worked for 67 years

While Fair is American’s most senior active flight attendant, it’s worth noting that she’s not the most senior American flight attendant ever. American’s most senior flight attendant ever — and for that matter, the industry’s most senior flight attendant ever — was Bette Nash.

She started her career in 1957, and she worked at the airlines for 67 years, up until 2024. She then passed away at the age of 88 . She was also recognized by Guinness World Records for being the world’s longest serving flight attendant.
Super senior flight attendants can be a mixed bag

There’s definitely a lot of ageism out there when it comes to how people perceive old flight attendants. Former Qatar Airways CEO Akbar Al Baker made headlines years back, when he talked about “crap American carriers” and how “you’re being served by grandmothers,” while bragging about how the average age of “his” flight attendants was only 26.

I think there are also a fair number of people who are just genuinely confused. If you’re from somewhere like Singapore or Japan, it’s just shocking to see people working in such a position at such an age.

I find that at airlines, super senior flight attendants are often on both ends of the spectrum in terms of quality. Some are just incredible, have such a good attitude, and really are a throwback to what service used to be like. Others, meanwhile, have an attitude, and clearly don’t want to be there.

As you’d expect, peoples’ motivation for wanting to work that long also varies. For some people, they genuinely enjoy their jobs, and it keeps them active, and they wouldn’t know what to do with themselves in retirement. For others, sadly they have to work to make ends meet, given how expensive life can be, and the lack of proper pensions.

When we’re talking about really senior flight attendants, my only concern is their ability to perform important safety duties. We always hear how flight attendants at US carriers are there primarily for our safety. However, there’s no denying that at a certain point, it becomes challenging to perform these duties.

Yes, senior flight attendants have to go through recurrent training, where they practice emergency evacuations, etc. However, they can take this multiple times if they fail. And there was a story many years ago about United’s most senior flight attendant at the time, and how many times she failed before passing. Obviously that’s a bit concerning.

American Airlines’ most senior flight attendant is retiring at the age of 83, after a career lasting over 63 years. She first started at Piedmont, then US Airways, and then American, thanks to three sets of mergers. On Monday, she’ll operate her last flight from London to Charlotte. Congrats to Fair, and may she have some enjoyable and healthy years in retirement!
body_zh: 在美国，各个年龄段的空乘人员都很常见。担任空乘人员没有最高年龄限制，只要您每年能够通过复训即可。该系统还极大地激励你在资历较高时留下来，因为你的工资已经达到顶峰，并可以根据资历进行竞价，选择路线。
沿着这些思路，美国航空目前最资深的空乘人员即将退休，我认为这是一个有趣的故事。
美国83岁空姐在工作63年后退休

泰德·里德 (Ted Reed) 讲述了美国航空最资深的空乘人员卡罗尔·费尔 (Carol Fair) 将于 2026 年 10 月 26 日星期一退休，届时她将乘坐最后一趟从伦敦 (LHR) 飞往夏洛特 (CLT) 的航班。这位 83 岁的老人于 1963 年在皮埃蒙特航空公司 (Piedmont Airlines) 开始了她的职业生涯，之后在全美航空公司 (US Airways) 工作，然后又在美国航空公司 (考虑到所有的合并)。因此，她将在超过 63 年的职业生涯后退休。
费尔即将退休，他是美国航空资历名单上排名第一的现役空乘人员，该名单包括约 30,000 人。从技术上讲，她只是该航空公司第三位最资深的空乘人员，但两位最资深的空乘人员不再飞行，但还没有正式退休。有趣的是，当费尔刚开始她的职业生涯时，她被美国航空拒绝了，因为该航空公司声称她“不是美国人”。然而，两次合并后，她来到了她最初希望工作的航空公司。
预计该航空公司将于周一在夏洛特降落时向费尔致敬，这一荣誉通常是为最后一次飞行的飞行员而不是空乘人员保留的。当费尔回顾她的职业生涯时，她分享了以下内容：
“是时候了。我很享受其中的每一分钟。我在三万名中排名第一。你不能再更高了，所以我还是把它挂掉吧。”
正如您所料，Fair 主要运营国际航班，因为这是积累大量时间并最大限度减少工作天数的最简单方法。她还解释说，与国内航班相比，她更喜欢乘客的质量，并表示“他们的通风更好。”哈。
美国最资深空姐已工作67年
虽然费尔是美国最资深的现役空乘人员，但值得注意的是，她并不是美国有史以来最资深的空乘人员。美国航空有史以来最资深的空乘人员——就此而言，也是该行业有史以来最资深的空乘人员——是贝蒂·纳什 (Bette Nash)。
她于 1957 年开始职业生涯，在航空公司工作了 67 年，直至 2024 年。随后去世，享年 88 岁。她还被吉尼斯世界纪录认定为世界上服务时间最长的空乘人员。
超级高级空姐鱼龙混杂
当谈到人们如何看待老年空乘人员时，肯定存在很多年龄歧视。卡塔尔航空前首席执行官阿克巴尔·阿尔·贝克（Akbar Al Baker）几年前就登上了头条新闻，当时他谈到“糟糕的美国航空公司”以及“你是如何享受祖母般的服务”，同时吹嘘“他的”空乘人员的平均年龄只有 26 岁。
我认为也有相当多的人确实感到困惑。如果你来自新加坡或日本这样的地方，看到人们在这样的年龄从事这样的职位，真是令人震惊。
我发现在航空公司，高级空乘人员的素质往往处于两端。有些真是令人难以置信，态度如此好，而且真的是回到了过去的服务。与此同时，其他人则持有一种态度，显然不想在那里。
正如您所料，人们想要工作这么长时间的动机也各不相同。对于一些人来说，他们真的很喜欢自己的工作，这让他们保持活力，而且他们不知道退休后该怎么办。对于其他人来说，可悲的是，鉴于生活成本高昂且缺乏适当的养老金，他们必须工作才能维持收支平衡。

Jetstar and Qantas have banned an Australian social media personality from flying with their airlines after he deliberately inflated an emergency life jacket during a pre-flight safety demonstration aboard a Jetstar flight from Sydney to Adelaide.

Hugh Lovett, one of the four brothers behind the Australian TikTok account The Lovetts, pulled the inflation cord on his life jacket aboard flight JQ768 on 16 October. The incident was filmed and subsequently shared on social media, showing the vest rapidly inflating as the recorded safety briefing instructed passengers to inflate their life jackets only after leaving the aircraft. The stunt reportedly formed part of content created for the brothers’ social media account.

Australian Federal Police officers met the aircraft after it arrived in Adelaide and escorted Lovett from the aircraft. The Qantas Group subsequently imposed a ban preventing him from travelling on both Qantas and Jetstar services. The duration of the ban has not been disclosed.

A Jetstar spokesperson said passengers are legally required to follow crew safety instructions and must not remove or tamper with emergency equipment unless instructed to do so. The airline added that it has zero tolerance for behaviour that puts passengers or crew at risk.

Emergency life jackets are designed to be inflated only after passengers have exited an aircraft during an evacuation over water. Inflating one inside the cabin can restrict movement, obstruct access to emergency exits and potentially slow the evacuation process. In the event of flooding, the buoyancy of an inflated vest can also make it more difficult for a passenger to move underwater towards an exit.

The Flemish Government has invoked a conflict of interest against the proposed changes to flight procedures at Brussels Airport, introduced by federal Mobility Minister Jean-Luc Crucke, arguing that the measures could shift aircraft noise from Brussels to the Flemish Rand. The decision was announced on Friday, 23 October, by Flemish Minister-President Matthias Diependaele. Referring the matter to Belgium’s Consultative Committee (Overlegcomité) suspends the implementation of Crucke’s decision for 60 days, a period that can in principle be extended by a further 60 days.

Crucke presented his plan earlier this month with the aim of reducing aircraft noise over northern Brussels. Under the proposal, aircraft arriving via runway 07L would enter Brussels airspace at a higher altitude and follow a steeper approach. The plan also includes changes to the wind criteria governing runway use, potentially reducing the number of aircraft using the 07L approach. However, the Flemish Government argues that changing these criteria could redirect traffic and noise towards other areas, including the northern and eastern outskirts of Brussels in Flanders.

“ Those who share the benefits of the airport must also help distribute the burden fairly ,” Diependaele said, insisting that the consequences of changes to flight procedures must be thoroughly assessed, with aviation safety and the interests of residents taken into account. He also criticised the lack of prior consultation between the federal and regional authorities, arguing that a balanced distribution of aircraft noise is essential.

Flemish Minister for the Environment Jo Brouns also opposed measures that could transfer noise pollution to the Flemish Rand or interfere with the ongoing procedure for a new environmental permit for Brussels Airport. Flemish Minister Ben Weyts had already threatened to invoke a conflict of interest earlier this month following the presentation of Crucke’s plans.

The dispute adds another layer to the long-running debate over the distribution of aircraft noise around Brussels Airport, which is located in Flanders but serves the wider Brussels region and Belgium’s international transport network. The Flemish Government says it wants the different authorities to consult one another before changes are implemented.

主页 机场 布鲁塞尔机场 (BRU) 弗拉芒政府因噪音问题暂停布鲁塞尔机场新的航班计划

佛兰德斯政府以利益冲突为由，反对联邦交通部部长让-吕克·克鲁克(Jean-Luc Crucke)提出的布鲁塞尔机场飞行程序变更提议，认为这些措施可能会将飞机噪音从布鲁塞尔转移到弗兰德斯。佛兰德部长兼总统马蒂亚斯·迪彭代勒 (Matthias Diependaele) 于 10 月 23 日星期五宣布了这一决定。将此事提交给比利时咨询委员会（Overlegcomité），将克鲁克的决定暂停执行 60 天，原则上可以再延长 60 天。
克鲁克本月早些时候提出了他的计划，旨在减少布鲁塞尔北部上空的飞机噪音。根据该提案，通过 07L 跑道抵达的飞机将以更高的高度进入布鲁塞尔空域，并采用更陡峭的进近路线。该计划还包括更改管理跑道使用的风力标准，这可能会减少使用 07L 进场的飞机数量。然而，佛兰德斯政府认为，改变这些标准可能会将交通和噪音转向其他地区，包括佛兰德斯布鲁塞尔的北郊和东郊。
迪彭代勒说：“那些分享机场利益的人也必须帮助公平地分配负担。”他坚持认为，必须彻底评估飞行程序变化的后果，同时考虑到航空安全和居民的利益。他还批评联邦和地区当局之间缺乏事先协商，认为飞机噪音的平衡分配至关重要。
弗拉芒环境部长乔·布劳恩斯也反对可能将噪音污染转移到弗拉芒兰特或干扰正在进行的布鲁塞尔机场新环境许可证程序的措施。本月早些时候，在克鲁克提出计划后，弗拉芒部长本·韦茨 (Ben Weyts) 就曾威胁要引发利益冲突。
这场争端为关于布鲁塞尔机场周围飞机噪音分布的长期争论增添了新的层面。该机场位于佛兰德斯，但服务于更广泛的布鲁塞尔地区和比利时的国际运输网络。弗拉芒政府表示，希望不同当局在实施改变之前相互协商。
资料来源：VRT NWS (Rik Arnoudt) 和 Het Laatste Nieuws (Laura Hamers)，2026 年 10 月 23 日。Aviation24.be 报道，包括之前对减少布鲁塞尔上空飞机噪音的联邦计划及其对周边地区的潜在影响的报道。

title_en: Philippine Airlines Mabuhay Lounge Manila Airport Review: The Wi-Fi Doesn’t Even Work
title_zh: 菲律宾航空Mabuhay休息室马尼拉机场评论：Wi-Fi甚至无法使用
summary: A review of the Philippine Airlines Mabuhay Lounge at Manila Terminal 1, where transit security was slow, the lounge was packed, and Wi-Fi wouldn't connect on a laptop.
summary_zh: 马尼拉 1 号航站楼菲律宾航空 Mabuhay 休息室的点评，那里的过境安检速度很慢，休息室挤满了人，而且 Wi-Fi 也无法使用
body_en: During my first class quest to Japan , I had the chance to spend some time in the Philippine Airlines Mabuhay Lounge Manila Airport (MNL). I had a roughly four hour layover, as I had arrived in Philippine Airlines’ A330 business class from Osaka (KIX) , and was connecting to Philippine Airlines’ A350 business class to San Francisco (SFO).

On the plus side, I didn’t have to switch terminals this time around, because a terminal change in Manila makes for what’s possibly the world’s worst airport transit experience . However, that’s not to say that the layover was smooth — quite to the contrary, I found the entire ground experience to be pretty bad . Transit security was a mess, and the lounge was overcrowded, with some major shortcomings.

Some may think my review here is overly critical, but let me simply state that somehow the lounge Wi-Fi doesn’t work on “foreign” computers (based on my experience, and confirmed by an airline employee), and that’s just mind-boggling to me. So if you want to use Wi-Fi on your laptop, you actually have to leave the lounge and go into the terminal, and use the airport free Wi-Fi. That’s just beyond embarrassing. Anyway, enough of an intro, let me get into the review.

Fortunately my Philippine Airlines flights were both arriving at and departing from Terminal 1 in Manila, so at least I didn’t have to switch terminals. All international connecting passengers have to clear transit security, and I found this to be a mess.

There was a long queue, and the entire space is set up with a single x-ray machine and metal detector. The line shown below also doesn’t account for the endless passengers in wheelchairs cutting the line (nothing against them, of course, but it all slows things down). There was also no sense of urgency among the screeners. It took roughly 40 minutes from the time I deplaned until I was through transit security.

I understand that airlines don’t have full control over airport facilities like this, but it’s really something that airport authorities need to work on. Philippine Airlines is growing, and in particular, is trying to increasingly compete with international connecting traffic. This is just such an avoidable pain point, especially when you consider the short connections the airline sells.

Admittedly most hub airports get busy during peak hours, but Manila Airport Terminal 1 is a special kind of mess. The terminal is narrow, and I found the signage confusing. Typically if you’re at a carrier’s hub terminal, it’s not too hard to find lounges. So I followed the signage in the direction of “Airline Lounges,” only to end up on the wrong side of the terminal.
As it turns out, the other direction also has signage for “Airline Lounges,” so you’d think they could have signage indicating which lounges are in which direction.
The Philippine Airlines Mabuhay Lounge is located near gate 15, though it’s honestly easy to miss.

There’s a sign for flights to Australia, and next to that is a sign where the biggest word is “Mabuhay,” and that’s the sign for the lounge. I walked past this area twice before I realized this is where the lounge was located. Again, for a hub lounge, you’d think they could do a bit better on signage.

The lounge is located on level four, which is one floor above the terminal. It can only be accessed via an elevator that’s in absolutely horrible condition (physically, and in terms of the feeling when riding it).

Once on level four, the entrance to the lounge was easy to spot. I have to say, my first impression was very positive, as the entrance is beautiful. For a moment I thought I’d actually have a nice lounge experience!

The Philippine Airlines Mabuhay Lounge Manila is open 24/7, as I understand it. Some reports online suggest it closes for a couple of hours in the middle of the night on Wednesdays for “maintenance.” But big picture, you really don’t have to worry about the hours of this lounge — if you have a flight, it’ll be open!
Philippine Airlines Lounge Manila entry requirements

The Philippine Airlines Mabuhay Lounge Manila has pretty straightforward access requirements. The lounge is open to Philippine Airlines business class passengers (no guests allowed) and Mabuhay Miles Premier Elite and Elite travelers (one guest allowed). On top of that, those without lounge access can purchase access at an additional cost, which varies based on the length of stay, and is subject to capacity limits.
Philippine Airlines Lounge Manila seating & layout

The Philippine Airlines Mabuhay Lounge Manila opened in late 2023, and it’s approximately 1,200 square meters (13,000 square feet), with a capacity for just under 300 guests. As is the case with any lounge, your experience will vary based on when you visit, and I definitely visited during a peak crowding period. The lounge is set along one main corridor, with a few main rooms.
When you enter the lounge, the first main room just has traditional lounge seating intended for relaxing. This consists mostly of chairs in rows, along with some tables.
Then in the back of the lounge is an area with dining tables, and this is also where the buffet is located.
Along the side of the lounge is a small room that’s more intended for resting, as it has some chairs with ottomans.
body_zh: 在前往日本的头等舱之旅中，我有机会在马尼拉机场 (MNL) 的菲律宾航空 Mabuhay 休息室度过了一段时间。我从大阪 (KIX) 搭乘菲律宾航空 A330 商务舱抵达，并转乘菲律宾航空 A350 商务舱飞往旧金山 (SFO)，因此中转时间大约为四个小时。
从好的方面来说，这次我不必更换航站楼，因为马尼拉的航站楼更换可能会带来世界上最糟糕的机场过境体验。不过，这并不是说转机很顺利，恰恰相反，我发现整个地面体验相当糟糕。过境安检一团糟，休息室人满为患，存在一些重大缺陷。
有些人可能认为我在这里的评论过于批评，但让我简单地说一下，不知何故，休息室 Wi-Fi 无法在“外国”计算机上运行（根据我的经验，并得到航空公司员工的证实），这让我难以置信。因此，如果您想在笔记本电脑上使用Wi-Fi，您实际上必须离开休息室并进入航站楼，并使用机场的免费Wi-Fi。这简直太尴尬了。无论如何，介绍已经够多了，让我开始评论吧。
幸运的是，我乘坐的菲律宾航空航班都是在马尼拉 1 号航站楼起降的，所以至少我不用换航站楼。所有国际转机乘客都必须通过过境安检，我发现这很乱。
排队的人很长，整个空间里只有一台X光机和金属探测器。下面显示的线路也没有考虑到无数坐着轮椅的乘客插队的情况（当然，这并不是反对他们，但这一切都会减慢速度）。安检人员也没有紧迫感。从我下飞机到通过过境安检大约花了 40 分钟。
我知道航空公司无法完全控制此类机场设施，但这确实是机场当局需要努力的事情。菲律宾航空公司正在不断发展，特别是正在努力与国际转机运输进行日益激烈的竞争。这正是一个可以避免的痛点，尤其是当您考虑到航空公司销售的短途航班时。
诚然，大多数枢纽机场在高峰时段都很繁忙，但马尼拉机场 1 号航站楼却特别混乱。航站楼很窄，而且我发现标牌很混乱。通常，如果您在航空公司的枢纽航站楼，找到休息室并不难。于是我按照指示牌朝“航空公司休息室”的方向走去，结果却走到了航站楼的错误一侧。
事实证明，另一个方向也有“航空公司休息室”的标牌，所以你可能会认为他们可能有标牌来指示哪些休息室位于哪个方向。
菲律宾航空 Mabuhay 休息室位于 15 号登机口附近，但老实说很容易错过。
有一个飞往澳大利亚的航班的标志，旁边有一个标志，最大的单词是“Mabuhay”，这就是休息室的标志。我走过这个区域两次才意识到这是休息室所在的地方。同样，对于枢纽休息室，您会认为他们可以在标牌上做得更好一些。
休息室位于四楼，即航站楼上方一层。它只能通过电梯进入，电梯的状况绝对糟糕（身体上，以及乘坐时的感觉）。
到了四楼，休息室的入口就很容易找到。我不得不说，我的第一印象非常积极，因为入口很漂亮。有那么一刻，我以为我真的会享受一次愉快的休息室体验！
据我了解，菲律宾航空马尼拉 Mabuhay 休息室 24/7 全天候开放。网上的一些报道表明，它会在周三半夜关闭几个小时以进行“维护”。但总的来说，你真的不必担心这个休息室的营业时间——如果你有航班，它就会开放！
菲律宾航空马尼拉休息室进入要求
菲律宾航空马尼拉马布海休息室的准入要求非常简单。休息室向菲律宾航空商务舱乘客（不允许携带任何乘客）和 Mabuhay Miles Premier Elite 和 Elite 旅客（允许一名乘客）开放。最重要的是，那些没有休息室使用权的人可以支付额外费用购买使用权，费用根据入住时间的长短而有所不同，并且受到容量限制。

summary_zh: 巴西制造商巴西航空工业公司 (Embraer) 在 2026 年第三季度全公司范围内的积压订单达到了创纪录的 357 亿美元……
body_en: Brazilian manufacturer Embraer has reached a record company-wide backlog of $35.7 billion during the third quarter of 2026, up 3% from the previous three months.
On October 23, 2026, Embraer declared that the third quarter had been marked by “strong commercial activity,” with sizeable firm orders for E-Jets from both Abra Group and ANA Holdings.
During the third quarter, with its commercial aviation sector, Embraer logged 36 firm orders and 30 purchase rights or options for its E2-family.
The company’s Executive Aviation division also posted a record-high $8.2 billion backlog, up 5% from the second quarter of 2026.
The period was notable for the launch of the Phenom 300EV and delivery of the first Praetor 600E to launch customer Flexjet.
In Defense and Security, the backlog reached $6.1 billion in the third quarter, a 56% increase from the same period in 2025.
Among the highlights, the Fuerza Aeroespacial Colombiana (FAC) ordered two KC-390 Millennium multi-mission aircraft in August 2026, worth around $366.4 million.
Embraer currently has 43 firm orders for KC-390 Millennium military transport, plus 25 for A-29 Super Tucano light attack aircraft.
With nine months of the year now having passed, Embraer has delivered 52 commercial aircraft. The company is aiming to deliver between 80 and 85 in total by the end of the year.
Overall, 115 executive aircraft have been delivered to customers so far this year. Embraer hopes to deliver between 160 and 170.
According to Embraer, across executive and commercial units, it has delivered approximately 67% of the full‑year guidance, which was set at between 240 and 255 aircraft for 2026.

Typhoon Champi has disrupted air travel across Taiwan, forcing the cancellation of more than 600 flights on Friday, 23 October, as authorities prepare for strong winds and torrential rain. All 262 domestic flights and more than 350 international services were cancelled, according to Taiwan’s transport ministry. Schools and offices were also closed across most of the island, while financial markets suspended trading.

The storm, which previously reached super-typhoon strength with winds approaching 300 km/h, has weakened but remains dangerous. Taiwan’s Central Weather Administration placed its centre approximately 330 kilometres east of the island’s southern tip on Friday, with gusts of around 191 km/h reported near the storm’s centre. Champi is expected to pass off northeastern Taiwan before turning towards the Chinese coast and eventually southern Japan, although its large circulation continues to affect a broad area.

The disruption extends beyond Taiwan. Airlines have cancelled or rescheduled services linking Taiwan with Japan, while carriers including HK Express have suspended flights between Hong Kong and Taiwanese destinations. Japan has also experienced flight cancellations and power outages as the storm approaches its southwestern islands. Authorities in Taiwan reported at least one death and dozens of injuries as of Friday, with evacuations carried out in areas at risk from flooding and landslides. Airlines are advising passengers to check their flight status before travelling.

台风“占比”迫使台湾600多个航班取消
台风“占比”扰乱了台湾各地的航空旅行，迫使 10 月 23 日星期五取消 600 多个航班，当局正在为强风和暴雨做好准备。据台湾交通运输部称，所有 262 趟国内航班和 350 多趟国际航班均被取消。岛上大部分地区的学校和办公室也关闭，金融市场暂停交易。
这场风暴此前曾达到超强台风强度，风速接近 300 公里/小时，现已减弱，但仍然危险。台湾中央气象局周五将其中心定位在台湾南端以东约 330 公里处，据报道风暴中心附近阵风约为 191 公里/小时。预计占比将经过台湾东北部，然后转向中国海岸，最终转向日本南部，尽管其庞大的环流继续影响广泛的地区。
破坏范围超出了台湾。航空公司已取消或重新安排连接台湾与日本的航班，而包括香港快运航空在内的航空公司已暂停来往香港与台湾目的地的航班。随着风暴逼近日本西南部岛屿，日本也经历了航班取消和停电的情况。截至周五，台湾当局报告已造成至少一人死亡、数十人受伤，并在面临洪水和山体滑坡风险的地区进行了疏散。航空公司建议乘客在旅行前检查航班状态。
